## docs/prefill-scheduling-and-concurrency.md

Canonical source: [docs/prefill-scheduling-and-concurrency.md](docs/prefill-scheduling-and-concurrency.md)

# Prefill scheduling and concurrent execution on two RTX 5070 Ti cards

On an i7-5960X with 64 GiB RAM, a PNY RTX 5070 Ti and an ASUS Prime RTX 5070 Ti,
the measured execution strategy matters as much as the number of installed cards.
Independent instances improve the five-job throughput of models that fit on each
card. A tested fair-prefill scheduler makes prompt admission and streaming more
consistent, while increasing the first-token wait for early requests. An explicit
Q8 K/V configuration demonstrates a larger Qwen27 workload with verified cache
precision and full GPU layer offload.

This study contains **19 valid performance conditions, one measured request group
per condition**, plus separate correctness checks. It uses a distinct diagnostic
protocol and does not modify or enter the canonical machine benchmark aggregates.
See the [raw evidence and reproduction guide](results/studies/20261106-prefill-scheduling/README.md),
[CSV](results/studies/20261106-prefill-scheduling/summary.csv),
[capture manifest](results/studies/20261106-prefill-scheduling/manifest.json), and
the existing [two-card placement study](docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md).

## What sequential-looking prefill means

In the pinned llama.cpp scheduler, generated tokens enter the logical batch first.
Pending prompts then fill the remaining batch in slot order. One unfinished prompt
can consume that entire remaining budget. Continuous batching permits decode and
prefill to mix; it does not guarantee equal prompt progress across requests.
The [upstream scheduler](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b12058/tools/server/server-context.cpp#L3978)
implements this policy. Qwen's hybrid memory implementation supports multiple
sequences with equal-length physical microbatches; its architecture does not
fundamentally require one prompt at a time.

Logical batch size and physical microbatch size are separate controls. Large
logical batches can reduce scheduling overhead while extending pauses in existing
streams. Large physical microbatches can increase memory requirements and reduce
opportunities to overlap pipeline stages across cards. GPU utilization describes
observed activity, not the fraction of advertised arithmetic throughput achieved.

## Controlled scheduler comparison

All rows below use the same Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M file, five matched approximately 20k
prompts, F16 K/V, 256 generated tokens per request, disabled speculation, and the
same experimental binary with the scheduler quota enabled or disabled. Startup
confirms **66/66 offloadable layers on GPU** and pipeline parallelism enabled.
Embeddings remain CPU-mapped. Requests use explicit IPv4 and a common dispatch gate.

First-output times below are offsets from that common gate. Individual client
TTFTs and dispatch offsets are retained separately in the raw capture.

| Prompt policy; logical / physical batch | Group completion | Total output tok/s | First / median / last first output | Largest observed stream-chunk gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Greedy; 2048 / 512 | 77.42 s | 16.53 | 9.77 / 33.47 / 66.52 s | 2.07 s |
| Fair; 2048 / 512, quota 512 | 69.99 s | 18.29 | 58.49 / 58.82 / 58.82 s | 0.33 s |
| Greedy; 8192 / 512 | 69.52 s | 18.41 | 20.76 / 42.80 / 58.31 s | 6.82 s |
| Fair; 8192 / 512, quota 2048 | 68.23 s | 18.76 | 56.62 / 57.02 / 57.03 s | 0.40 s |
| Greedy; 2048 / 2048 | 91.66 s | 13.96 | 9.66 / 40.52 / 80.74 s | 2.66 s |

![Actual request timing with greedy and fair admission](results/studies/20261106-prefill-scheduling/figures/request-timelines.svg)

At the 2048/512 setting, fair admission increases measured group throughput by
10.6% and reduces the last first-output wait by 11.6%. However, median first-output
wait increases by 75.7%. The corresponding measured GPU energy falls only 1.1%,
from 24.54 to 24.27 J/output token; this single observation does not establish a
robust energy advantage. At 5k, throughput rises 3.3%, but energy/token increases 1.4%.

The tuned greedy 8192 condition approaches fair 8192's aggregate throughput, while
retaining longer streaming pauses. Fair admission is therefore a policy choice
for consistent progress and smoother responses, rather than a universal latency
optimization. Stream-chunk gaps are client-observed arrival intervals, not GPU
token-generation intervals. After-first-token decode rates include scheduler waits.

Increasing the physical microbatch to 2048 slows this 20k cohort and raises combined
peak VRAM from 25,223 to 28,875 MiB. Keep logical and physical batch tuning separate.

## Independent instances versus splitting one model

Each row submits five approximately 20k prompts and generates exactly 1,280 output
tokens in total. Within each model, weights, prompt hashes/counts, F16 K/V,
sampling, output policy and CPU thread settings match. Full GPU layer offload and
zero reported prompt-cache reuse are verified.

The replica strategy loads one complete model on each GPU, with **one backend
slot per instance**. Five submitted clients queue three jobs on the PNY card and
two on the ASUS card. It does not execute five decoders simultaneously. Energy
covers both installed cards over one group window, including idle portions.

| Model and execution | Group time | Total output tok/s | GPU J/output token | Combined peak VRAM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LFM2.5-24B QAD-Q4_0; PNY only, one slot | 20.31 s | 63.04 | 4.005 | 14,325 MiB |
| Same LFM; two-card layer split, five slots | 21.95 s | 58.30 | 5.095 | 17,371 MiB |
| Same LFM; two replicas, one slot each | 12.50 s | 102.39 | 3.818 | 28,235 MiB |
| Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q3_K_XL; two-card layer split, five slots | 77.63 s | 16.49 | 23.854 | 21,807 MiB |
| Same Qwen27; two replicas, one slot each | 49.72 s | 25.74 | 17.993 | 27,922 MiB |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M; two-card layer split, five slots | 30.40 s | 42.11 | 7.796 | 24,672 MiB |

![Throughput and energy for the measured execution strategies](results/studies/20261106-prefill-scheduling/figures/replica-throughput-energy.svg)

For LFM, replication increases aggregate throughput 75.6% over layer splitting
and 62.4% over the single-card queue. Compared with splitting, it reduces measured
GPU energy/token 25.1%, while increasing average combined board power from 297 to
391 W and increasing VRAM occupancy. The five-job 3/2 distribution limits finite
cohort scaling even when both instances are efficient.

For Qwen27 Q3, replicas improve group throughput 56.1% and reduce measured GPU
energy/token 24.6% relative to splitting. Model replication avoids inter-card layer
dependencies, while consuming memory for two model copies. These are measured
serving-strategy results; they do not rank model quality or establish behavior at
arbitrary context lengths. Use the largest-model strategy when a complete copy
cannot fit on one card.

## LM Studio controls and context capacity

LM Studio 0.4.24 with the selected CUDA12 engine 2.70.0 was tested using server-reported
five-session, unified-KV, flash-attention, cache-precision and disabled-MTP settings.
Its documented load controls include batch size, flash attention and KV placement;
there is no documented fair-prefill scheduler control in the
[load API](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/rest/load).
The experimental scheduler patch operates in the separate llama.cpp build and
does not replace LM Studio's engine.

These 20k LM Studio rows use natural EOS with a 256-token maximum. Their output
counts differ, so throughput and joules/token do not isolate batch efficiency.

| Evaluation batch | Actual output tokens | Group time | First / median / last first output | Total measured GPU energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 1,192 | 55.61 s | 8.83 / 25.26 / 41.13 s | 22.09 kJ |
| 4096 | 1,243 | 53.40 s | 10.29 / 25.95 / 38.09 s | 21.83 kJ |
| 8192 | 1,249 | 51.76 s | 14.38 / 29.08 / 36.19 s | 21.52 kJ |

Batch 4096 is a measured compromise for this workload. Batch 8192 reduces the
last first-output wait further, while worsening early and median waits. Total GPU
energy spans 21.52–22.09 kJ across these different-output observations. None of these settings
makes LM Studio's prompt admission fair.

Explicit **Q8 cache precision**, retaining the Q4_K_M weights, demonstrates larger
usable workloads. The following 5x40k cases allocate 215,040 shared context tokens,
43,008 per slot, and both produce 1,280 output tokens successfully:

| Serving condition | K/V precision | Group time | Last first output | Combined peak VRAM | Peak GPU temperature |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LM Studio, batch 4096, natural EOS | Q8_0 | 114.47 s | 89.89 s | 28,893 MiB / 28.22 GiB | 77 C |
| Experimental llama.cpp fair 8192/512, fixed 256 output | Q8_0 | 199.34 s | 178.42 s | 27,901 MiB / 27.25 GiB | 78 C |

These are different serving conditions, not a scheduler-only paired comparison.
For reference, the earlier 5x40k LM Studio experiment, with unverified cache
precision, failed full-GPU loading and its CPU-fallback case completed only two of
five requests. Keep that historical observation separate: this is not a controlled
F16-versus-Q8 capacity comparison at 40k. Q8 changes cache arithmetic and requires its own quality
evaluation; it is not a free or verified quality-equivalent capacity increase.

## Reproduction, telemetry and limits

The performance binary uses upstream llama.cpp commit
`3f8af15a76ac8675812e856da45454bafc90f12c` with the optional
[v1 scheduler patch](results/studies/20261106-prefill-scheduling/patches/fair-prefill-v1.patch).
It was built using MSVC 19.39 with dynamic backends and the unchanged official
b12058 CUDA 13.4 backend/runtime DLLs. File hashes, build controls, weight hash,
actual request counts, slot progress, chunk arrivals, raw power samples and
per-card counter summaries are retained. Canonical prompts use explicit UTF-8;
submission hashes verify the actual HTTP input against the retained text. The release binary's separate 20k control
measured 16.63 tok/s versus 16.53 for the compiled quota-disabled control; scheduler
claims use the same compiled binary on both sides.

The [v2 patch](results/studies/20261106-prefill-scheduling/patches/fair-prefill-v2.patch)
adds explicit shared-parent/child exclusions. Its separate natural-stopping,
mixed-length unique-code checks pass 15/15 replies across greedy F16, fair F16 and
fair Q8. They test sequence isolation only. They are not a general capability or
quality-equivalence benchmark, and no performance gain is attributed to v2's guard.

Both cards negotiate PCIe Gen3 x16 during active dual-card work. PCIe counters
are driver-reported KB/s samples, not integrated transfer bytes. Shared-memory
allocations and global paging counters are captured; shared allocation alone does
not prove GPU spill or page-file traffic. CPU and RAM counters cover the whole
client machine. Per-process diagnostic counters are available for owned standalone
engines; LM Studio per-process attribution and a new kernel trace are not provided
by this campaign. CPU/package and memory-junction temperatures remain unavailable.

Measured inference die-temperature peaks across the campaign are 78 C on PNY and
66 C on ASUS. An 85 C stop guard monitors diagnostic engines. No temperature stop
occurred. Background model downloads were paused for timed collection. Model
weights used the existing SATA files; there is no Samsung 990 Pro measurement here.

Use these results by objective:

- **Early first response:** retain greedy admission and test moderate logical batches.
- **Smoother simultaneous streams:** evaluate the optional fair scheduler, accepting its early/median latency cost.
- **Aggregate job throughput:** use one replica per card when the full model and its per-instance context fit.
- **Larger tested context:** evaluate Q8 K/V as a separate condition; 5x40k is demonstrated here.
- **GPU energy:** compare complete matched-output groups; replication is the stronger measured improvement in this cohort.

For the application views and metric definitions, see
[Concurrency comparisons](docs/concurrency.md) and [Measurements and sessions](docs/measurements.md).

---

## docs/flash-next-quality.md

Canonical source: [docs/flash-next-quality.md](docs/flash-next-quality.md)

# Flash-Next task accuracy on two RTX 5070 Ti cards

This collection evaluates Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in the original Unsloth
`UD-IQ4_XS` and ISTA-DASLab `IQ3_S` packages on fixed public questions. Each question has one primary
generation, with its prompt, visible answer and deterministic grading retained.
These are **64-question samples**, separate from full-dataset or official
leaderboard results.

| Quantization | Suite | Correct / planned | Graded coverage | Accuracy | First-repeat descriptive 95% interval | Request errors / output limits |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS | ARC-Challenge, science multiple choice | 63 / 64 | 64 / 64 | 98.4% | 91.7–99.7% | 0 / 0 |
| Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS | GSM8K, math word problems | 63 / 64 | 64 / 64 | 98.4% | 91.7–99.7% | 0 / 0 |
| Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS | MMLU-Pro, 14 subjects | 54 / 64 | 64 / 64 | 84.4% | 73.6–91.3% | 0 / 0 |
| ISTA-DASLab IQ3_S | ARC-Challenge, science multiple choice | 64 / 64 | 64 / 64 | 100.0% | 94.3–100.0% | 0 / 0 |
| ISTA-DASLab IQ3_S | GSM8K, math word problems | 62 / 64 | 64 / 64 | 96.9% | 89.3–99.1% | 0 / 0 |
| ISTA-DASLab IQ3_S | MMLU-Pro, 14 subjects | 52 / 64 | 64 / 64 | 81.2% | 70.0–88.9% | 0 / 0 |

ARC and GSM8K are close to the ceiling; the MMLU-Pro sample produces more
answer-key mismatches. These results establish auditable performance
on the selected questions, with limited ability to resolve small differences
between configurations. Public benchmark questions may have appeared in
training. The interval is a descriptive Wilson approximation over distinct
first-repeat questions, rather than a model-ranking significance test or an
intelligence rating.

The same selected questions, prompts and grading rules are used for both
packages. Pairing individual answers gives the following descriptive comparison:

| Suite | Both correct | Only UD-IQ4_XS correct | Only IQ3_S correct | Both incorrect |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ARC-Challenge | 63 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| GSM8K | 62 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| MMLU-Pro | 51 | 3 | 1 | 9 |

Total scores differ by one or two answers per suite. They do not establish a
general quality ranking or quality equivalence. These are different publisher
packages, including different quantization recipes, rather than an isolated
bit-width experiment. Evaluate their throughput separately using the
[dual-card performance results](docs/two-5070-ti-comparison.md).

![ARC-Challenge accuracy and descriptive intervals for the two Flash-Next packages](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/accuracy-arc-challenge-test-chat-v1.png)

![GSM8K accuracy and descriptive intervals for the two Flash-Next packages](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/accuracy-gsm8k-test-chat-v1.png)

![MMLU-Pro balanced-subset accuracy and descriptive intervals for the two Flash-Next packages](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/accuracy-mmlu-pro-balanced64-chat-v1.png)

## Collection protocol

| Setting | Recorded condition |
| --- | --- |
| Machine | Intel Core i7-5960X, 64 GiB RAM, PNY plus ASUS Prime RTX 5070 Ti, 16 GiB per card, Windows |
| Engine | Native Strata 0.1.52; Strata Control owns model loading |
| Weights | Original [Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/tree/766911a6b7369840a91dbcd95f9f997acaab6cd6/UD-IQ4_XS) and [ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ3_S](https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF/tree/ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09); revisions retained in configuration metadata |
| Context / KV | 65,536 tokens / INT8 |
| Serving | One backend slot; both GPUs available to the native engine |
| Reasoning | Requested `none`; recorded native template control `enable_thinking:false` with a closed think prefix |
| MTP | Configured on, requested four draft tokens; activity observed in native engine logs. Public API configuration keeps requested, reported and unknown effective state separate |
| Expert policy | All selected experts participate; route-tail skipping disabled |
| Sampling | Temperature 0, top-p 1; one generation per selected question |
| Selection | ARC/GSM: 64 SHA-256-ranked IDs per split. MMLU-Pro: four or five questions per each of 14 subjects. Seed 73,129; selection is independent of answers or model results |
| Generation | 32,768-token total ceiling; no client wall-clock deadline; selection seed is not sent as an API generation seed |
| Grading | ARC and MMLU-Pro generated final letter; GSM8K final numeric answer; visible content only |

Native draft-count extracts retain all 193 request summaries per package:
one budget check followed by the 192 capability questions. Each question's
prompt and output counts match the corresponding engine summary in order.

| Package | Offered / accepted drafts | Request summaries | Extract and scope/hash record |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| UD-IQ4_XS | 108,685 / 77,430 | 193 | [Rows](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/ud4-native-draft-full193-rows.txt), [evidence](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/ud4-native-draft-full193-evidence.json) |
| IQ3_S | 102,931 / 73,098 | 193 | [Rows](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/iq3-native-draft-full193-rows.txt), [evidence](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/iq3-native-draft-full193-evidence.json) |

There is no zero-offer request in either extract. MTP is configured on, and
the engine also logs suffix drafting. The totals do not isolate mechanisms
or establish an MTP speed or quality benefit. Internal draft proposals are
not additional inference repeats. The initial
[124-summary UD-IQ4_XS extract](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/ud4-native-draft-rows.txt)
and its [scope record](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/ud4-native-draft-evidence.json)
remain available separately.

The full source splits contain 1,172 ARC-Challenge, 1,319 GSM8K and 12,032
MMLU-Pro questions. The fixed MMLU-Pro sample has a different subject weighting
from its full test split; it uses all 64 questions in the balanced suite.
These runs use the versioned zero-shot Wattever chat adaptations described in
[capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md). AI2 ARC-Challenge is a school-science
multiple-choice dataset, distinct from ARC-AGI grid reasoning. MMLU-Pro uses
zero-shot generated letters, separate from its official five-shot CoT protocol.

Background model downloading overlapped accuracy collection. **Do not use these
quality runs for speed or energy comparisons.** Per-question timings and
telemetry remain audit observations. The separate
[dual-card throughput study](docs/two-5070-ti-comparison.md) defines the performance
and energy comparison conditions.

## Inspect the answers

All answers marked incorrect completed naturally, with a valid final output. The UD-IQ4_XS ARC
answer selected fertilization where the source key selects maturation in a
plant-life-cycle question. The GSM8K answer split a dinner bill including its
tip, where the source key assigns the full tip to one payer. The recorded
decisions are answer-key mismatches, rather than truncated output or parser
failures. The source keys remain unchanged.

UD-IQ4_XS MMLU-Pro used 73,772 output tokens across 64 questions. Its longest response,
engineering item `mmlu-pro-test-11438`, used 10,522 tokens and ended naturally;
it was not truncated. The published question has compressed spacing and an
undefined variable `y`. Its recorded final answer disagrees with the source
key. The prompt and key remain unchanged: source ambiguity can limit the
interpretation of an individual answer-key mismatch.

Open **Capabilities** in the helper or hosted application to inspect published
question evidence. The raw files are independently importable:

- UD-IQ4_XS: [ARC64](results/capabilities/cap-20261104-011521-b0148a48af.json), [GSM64 derived coverage record](results/capabilities/cap-derived-20261104-ud4-gsm64-21b02ce673c2.json), [MMLU-Pro balanced64](results/capabilities/cap-20261104-021604-96f2560798.json).
- IQ3_S: [ARC64](results/capabilities/cap-20261104-031500-dd84d8fedb.json), [GSM64](results/capabilities/cap-20261104-032720-214f9e86df.json), [MMLU-Pro balanced64](results/capabilities/cap-20261104-034240-e076a5af10.json).
- [Summary CSV](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/summary.csv).

The GSM64 record is the exact union of two disjoint collection segments from
the same loaded engine instance and model configuration: 59 retained answers
and five previously unobserved questions. No question was generated twice.
All 64 answers are re-scored against the original fixed selection. Its
[59-answer source](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/ud4-source/cap-20261104-013428-1da798dd1e.json)
retains terminal status `error`; its
[five-answer source](results/aggregates/flash-next-quality/ud4-source/cap-20261104-021212-1ca9064533.json)
is complete. Input hashes, zero overlap, per-item provenance and separate
telemetry segments are recorded in the derived JSON. Segment references are
paths from the repository root. No joined duration, averaged rate or combined
energy is calculated.

Dataset-specific sources, attribution and licenses are in
[dataset provenance](corpora/capabilities/README.md). See
[sharing results](docs/sharing-results.md) for audit imports and public contributions.

## docs/experiment-status.md

Canonical source: [docs/experiment-status.md](docs/experiment-status.md)

# Dual RTX 5070 Ti experiment checkpoint

This checkpoint records the completed studies and GLM preparation on
2026-11-04. The machine has an i7-5960X, 64 GiB DDR4 and PNY plus ASUS Prime
RTX 5070 Ti cards, each with 16 GiB. Performance, capability evaluation,
transfer probes and profiled captures remain separate measurement families.

## Completed measurements

| Collection | Coverage | Published evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LM Studio and native Strata | 180 attempted cases: 179 successful, one retained timeout; one measured repeat per case | [Performance report](docs/two-5070-ti-comparison.md), [case CSV](results/aggregates/two-5070-ti-absolute-cases.csv) |
| Standalone llama.cpp placement and concurrency | 153 unprofiled conditions plus three separately labelled Gemma traces; successes, unsupported modes and failures retained | [Execution report](docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md), [raw diagnostic archive](results/aggregates/two-5070-ti-diagnostic-raw.json.gz) |
| Communication probes | 280 conditions across 14 routes, ten transfer sizes and two timing modes; internal samples are not inference repeats | [Transfer samples](results/aggregates/two-5070-ti-diagnostic-micro-samples.csv) |
| Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS accuracy | ARC64, GSM8K64 and MMLU-Pro64: 192 answers | [Quality report](docs/flash-next-quality.md) |
| Flash-Next IQ3_S accuracy | The same 192 questions; all answered once | [Quality audits and charts](docs/flash-next-quality.md) |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | Download and verified staging complete; runtime pack and measurements pending; **no inference or quality results collected** | Preparation scope below |

The hosted Results catalog contains **six hardware setups**, including the
dual-5070 setup. Engine sessions stay within their hardware entry. The
standalone diagnostics do not enter normal benchmark aggregates. Capabilities
contains six separate suite results for the two Flash-Next packages.
Nineteen diagnostic conditions retain download-overlap flags. Instrumented
captures and background-confounded observations remain outside clean inference
comparisons; their timing is not substituted for an unprofiled measurement.

## What two cards improve

These representative standalone results compare the same quantization and
backend on one 5070 Ti against balanced layer placement on both cards.
Numbers are client prefill / decode in tokens per second, at an 80k prompt
target. Actual prompt/output counts, contexts and settings remain in the
[execution report](docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md).

| Model and quant | One card | Both cards, balanced | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| LFM2.5-24B, Q4_0 QAD | 1,792 / 83.69 | 7,405 / 129.38 | Both phases improve; 256 output tokens in both cases |
| Qwen3.8-27B, Q3_K_XL | 449 / 1.41 | 2,010 / 36.42 | Large gain where the single-card placement spills weights; 221 output tokens in both cases |
| Qwen3.6-35B, Q4_K_M | 386 / 50.20 | 4,882 / 113.22 | Both phases improve; natural EOS gives 234 versus 233 output tokens |
| Gemma E2B, Q4_K_M | 7,304 / 152.66 | 5,645 / 10.60 | Equal splitting is a poor choice for this architecture |

Gemma's reversed weighted placement reaches 9,507 prefill and 111.66 decode
tokens/s: substantially better than its equal split, while single-card decode
remains faster. Shared-KV placement is a measured configuration difference;
the traces do not establish every causal contribution.

Independent LFM instances on separate cards at 20k/two clients improve measured
whole-job output throughput from 45.99 to 117.77 tokens/s. At 80k, balanced
placement instead provides 13.65 whole-job tokens/s versus 9.84 for independent
instances. Per-request rates are not added to manufacture simultaneous
throughput. Overlapping GPU energy is integrated once.

## Native Flash-Next performance and accuracy

The normal native-Strata cases below use one client. Each package is a
separate model condition; this is not an isolated bit-width comparison.

| Package | 20k prefill / decode | 80k prefill / decode | ARC64 | GSM8K64 | MMLU-Pro64 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS | 1,062.01 / 18.18 | 1,971.69 / 17.55 | 63 / 64 | 63 / 64 | 54 / 64 |
| ISTA-DASLab IQ3_S | 1,089.00 / 73.26 | 2,359.37 / 69.58 | 64 / 64 | 62 / 64 | 52 / 64 |

The accuracy runs have complete coverage, no request errors and no output
limits, with a 32,768-token generation budget. They use 65,536 context; the
separate normal performance cohort uses 98,304. Download activity overlapped
quality collection, so **quality timings and energy are not performance
measurements**. Small fixed public-question subsets cannot establish general
quality equivalence or an official leaderboard ranking. See the descriptive
intervals and individual answers in the [quality report](docs/flash-next-quality.md).

IQ3_S is the practical speed candidate among these measured native packages.
Its small sample-score differences from UD-IQ4_XS need wider evaluation before
making a general quality claim. Native Qwen35 used one GPU despite two being
installed, so its results do not establish a two-card acceleration.

## Communication and temperature

Both cards negotiated PCIe Gen3 x16 under load. CUDA peer access is unavailable
in both directions. Explicit host-staged copies are labelled as staged;
fallback copies are not reported as direct P2P.

| Measured route | Throughput |
| --- | ---: |
| Pinned RAM to PNY / ASUS, 256 MiB | 13.575 / 13.555 GB/s |
| PNY / ASUS to pinned RAM, 256 MiB | 10.387 / 10.418 GB/s |
| Explicit staged card 0 to 1 / 1 to 0 | 1.773 / 2.375 GB/s |
| Measured simultaneous equal-size RAM to both GPUs | 13.961 GB/s combined |
| Measured simultaneous weighted 2:1 RAM to both GPUs | 19.465 GB/s combined |
| Measured bidirectional cross-card traffic | 11.308 GB/s combined |

These values retain their sizes, timing methods, synchronization and validation
in the [transfer evidence](docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md). They are not sums of
independent rates. Link ceilings are not measured transfer rates.

The completed performance campaign reached 77°C on PNY and 67°C on ASUS, with
no observed hardware/software thermal-slowdown flags. GPU die observations do
not measure memory-junction temperature; that counter is unavailable. Per-card
power, clocks, utilization, energy and sample coverage remain published.

## GLM preparation and remaining work

The selected first candidate is **Maya-XS mixed IQ1_S/IQ2_XXS**, pinned to
quantizer revision `6728cf78a5b198a6a6f84b7fb88956a17ec56521`. Its two shards
total **73,411,389,088 bytes**. The official model publisher reports **320B
total / 18B active parameters**. The rounded parameter counts do not describe
the quantized file size.

The download completed on 2026-11-04. By 05:12 UTC, both shards had their full
publisher checksums verified on NVMe and on complete SATA backup copies.
The runtime compatibility pack has not been created. The
larger Maya-S24 package has not been downloaded or benchmarked.

The experimental runtime is **Project Maya v1.1.52**, source
`3c935e411cd6625a9af0f292dd0af52598e866d8`, built for the installed Windows/CUDA
environment. It is a Strata-derived backend, distinct from native Strata.
The vendor BF16 compatibility pack is a separate runtime treatment, so the
quantizer's published quality figures do not directly describe this experiment.

No GLM weights have been loaded, no GLM inference endpoint has been started,
and **there are no measured GLM prefill, decode, energy or accuracy scores**.
Runtime compilation and engine-free control checks establish preparation,
not working-model or performance evidence. Therefore no measured comparison
with Flash-Next or optimized GLM setting is claimed.

The remaining sequence is verified staging and pack creation; foreground
Strata Control loading; actual allocation, MTP, KV and output-budget checks;
one measured 20k/single-client case; then the missing cases in the six-context,
one/two-client matrix. RAM tiers, KV placement, MTP policy and serving slots
require separately identified conditions. Official GLM LOW reasoning must
remain separate from Maya's forced-off prompt treatment. Fixed capability
questions use the same source selections as the Flash-Next audits.

GLM source and model references: [official model](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash),
[quantizer](https://huggingface.co/peasantsmith/GLM-5.3-Flash-Maya-GGUF),
[Maya runtime](https://github.com/mw00/project-maya/tree/3c935e411cd6625a9af0f292dd0af52598e866d8).

## docs/5060-ti-storage-comparison.md

Canonical source: [docs/5060-ti-storage-comparison.md](docs/5060-ti-storage-comparison.md)

# RTX 5060 Ti: Strata SSD and NVMe comparison

Open **Results** and select **RTX 5060 Ti**. **Summary** shows coverage, machine-transfer rates and the recorded storage experiment. Choose **Compare recorded storage** to select both measured storage conditions and their models in **Compare**. Use **Recorded conditions**, **Measures**, **Queries** and **Models** to control the charts; choose an overlay or one chart per model. Switch to **Table** for the same selected measurements and expand **All measurements** for individual repeats and exact query token counts/timings. **Export CSV** exports the selected conditions, model and query count. The Summary experiment's **Export both conditions CSV** downloads all 144 baseline/alternative records.

The [benchmark JSON](results/runs/20261030-211908_rtx-5060-ti_af3694cca3.json) retains 312 primary Samsung cases plus 72 alternative NVMe observations in the same machine entry. `storage_comparison` contains frozen baseline and alternative rows, per-workload medians, a per-model summary, copy verification and comparison settings. Views use the primary Samsung measurements by default. Selecting NVMe adds its recorded observations without replacing the primary results.

## Measured inference effect

| Model / quant | Median completion speedup | Matched cases | Samsung passed | NVMe passed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen 3.6 35B A3B UD-Q4_K_XL | 1.002x | 24 | 24/24 | 24/24 |
| Flash Next IQ3_S | 1.013x | 24 | 24/24 | 24/24 |
| Flash Next UD-IQ4_XS | 1.745x | 22 | 22/24 | 24/24 |

Speedup is the median Samsung/NVMe wall-time ratio over matching successful cases across all six prompt sizes and both query counts. A timeout is excluded from that ratio. The following 80k values retain both individual repeats; seconds cover completion of all queries in the case.

| Model / quant | Queries | Samsung repeat 1 / 2 (s) | NVMe repeat 1 / 2 (s) |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Qwen 3.6 35B A3B UD-Q4_K_XL | 1 | 191.28 / 185.88 | 192.46 / 187.37 |
| Qwen 3.6 35B A3B UD-Q4_K_XL | 2 | 368.98 / 371.94 | 370.73 / 370.85 |
| Flash Next IQ3_S | 1 | 115.42 / 115.67 | 114.16 / 113.26 |
| Flash Next IQ3_S | 2 | 225.89 / 227.68 | 226.04 / 226.79 |
| Flash Next UD-IQ4_XS | 1 | 323.77 / 324.55 | 179.20 / 176.34 |
| Flash Next UD-IQ4_XS | 2 | timeout at 600s / skipped | 353.48 / 350.29 |

UD-IQ4_XS benefits substantially from NVMe, including successful 80k paired workloads. IQ3_S and Qwen 3.6 inference timings are essentially unchanged. The UD-IQ4_XS observation includes physical-drive I/O samples during inference; a faster sequential disk rate alone does not establish an inference benefit.

## Machine and transfer measurements

| Component / path | Recorded condition or median rate |
| --- | --- |
| GPU | RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB; PCIe 3 x8 under transfer |
| CPU / RAM | Intel i7-5820K; 64 GB; firmware reports 2133 MT/s; BIOS unchanged |
| Samsung SSD 870 EVO SATA to RAM | 0.54 GB/s |
| AirDisk NVMe (F:) to RAM | 2.82 GB/s |
| RAM copy, one / six workers | 9.93 / 20.63 GB/s copied payload |
| Pinned RAM to VRAM | 6.58 GB/s |

The sequential NVMe read probe is 5.23x faster. RAM copy payload throughput is not peak DRAM bus bandwidth. All 78 copied files (195.7 GiB) passed source-stream and destination-readback SHA256 checks; Samsung originals remain available.

## Comparison conditions

- Six targets: 512, 5k, 10k, 20k, 40k and 80k; one/two simultaneous clients; two repeats; 256 output-token limit; 600-second case limit. Actual input/output counts remain in the raw query records.
- Same model files, quantizations, 98,304-token engine context and Strata 0.1.52. MTP is requested/reported on; effective execution remains unknown where native counters do not establish it. One backend slot queues the two clients.
- Flash Next uses the same 40 GiB host expert-cache cap on both drives, with observed pageable fallback after Windows refused the pinned allocation. The historical 5070 Ti benchmark used automatic host residency. Its [new controlled storage follow-up](docs/5070-ti-hardware-follow-up.md) separately measures both drives with a 40 GiB cap, preserving those older rows.
- Native Qwen 3.6 matches 21 GPU experts per layer and 18.75 GiB pinned host residency. The requested GPU budget is 3 GiB on Samsung and 2.65 GiB on NVMe to preserve that effective placement.
- OS standby caches were not forcibly flushed. Model-loading observations are not controlled cold-start timings. Two repeats describe these workloads; they do not establish universal speedup or statistical significance.

See [measurement definitions](docs/measurements.md) for client timing, concurrency and cache boundaries.

## docs/5070-ti-hardware-follow-up.md

Canonical source: [docs/5070-ti-hardware-follow-up.md](docs/5070-ti-hardware-follow-up.md)

# RTX 5070 Ti: hardware and paired storage follow-up

The [5070 Ti benchmark JSON](results/runs/20261031-165925_rtx-5070-ti_57b747d701.json) now contains **144 completed storage observations**, three independent transfer captures, memory-topology evidence and a PCIe diagnostic. All 144 latest storage observations passed. The original 312 inference rows, sessions and engine groups are preserved. One earlier 600-second timeout remains in the attempt history.

Open **Results**, select **RTX 5070 Ti**, then **Compare recorded storage**. The charts select the fresh SATA control and NVMe condition; the older automatic-residency measurements remain separate. Select **Prefill speed** and **Decode speed** for separate charts. Change **Simultaneous queries** to inspect either client count. **Table** retains individual repeats and request timings. **Export both conditions CSV** downloads all 144 raw observations.

The [aggregate CSV](results/aggregates/rtx-5070-ti-storage.csv) contains all 36 model/size/client-count groups: two repeats, medians and ranges for prefill, decode and wall time, actual token counts, case limits and drafting observations.

## Inference results

Completion speedup is the median of matched SATA/NVMe case wall-time ratios over six prompt targets, both client counts and two repeats. It describes this workload mix, rather than aggregate tokens per second.

| Model / quant | Median completion speedup | Matched cases | SATA passed | NVMe passed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS | 1.842x | 24 | 24/24 | 24/24 |
| Flash-Next IQ3_S | 0.998x | 24 | 24/24 | 24/24 |
| Qwen3.6 35B A3B UD-Q4_K_XL | 1.006x | 24 | 24/24 | 24/24 |

NVMe substantially improved UD-IQ4_XS in this configuration. IQ3_S and Qwen3.6 were essentially unchanged. Faster sequential storage does not imply the same inference gain for models with different residency and caching behavior.

### 80k target, one client

Values are medians of two successful repeats. Prefill and decode use client timings; wall time covers the completed request.

| Model / quant | SATA prefill / decode (tok/s) | NVMe prefill / decode (tok/s) | SATA wall (s) | NVMe wall (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS | 262.0 / 9.8 | 555.1 / 11.7 | 329.12 | 163.04 |
| Flash-Next IQ3_S | 1,440.0 / 22.7 | 1,457.0 / 22.5 | 64.35 | 62.74 |
| Qwen3.6 35B A3B UD-Q4_K_XL | 1,059.4 / 12.0 | 1,075.1 / 12.3 | 94.71 | 92.92 |

### 80k target, two clients

One backend slot queues the two clients. Prefill uses each case's median per-request rate, then the median across repeats. It includes queue delay in time to first token and must not be read as isolated engine prefill throughput. Wall time covers both completed requests.

| Model / quant | SATA prefill / decode (tok/s) | NVMe prefill / decode (tok/s) | SATA wall (s) | NVMe wall (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS | 191.7 / 9.8 | 379.2 / 11.6 | 660.75 | 345.45 |
| Flash-Next IQ3_S | 1,053.9 / 24.0 | 1,056.6 / 22.5 | 126.99 | 129.45 |
| Qwen3.6 35B A3B UD-Q4_K_XL | 777.0 / 12.3 | 776.9 / 12.4 | 183.53 | 184.05 |

## Experimental controls

- Three models, two storage volumes, targets 512/5k/10k/20k/40k/80k, one/two clients and two repeats: 144 observations. Engine context was verified at 98,304 tokens before every condition. Output limit was 256; actual lengths can be shorter and are retained. Reasoning effort was requested as `none`, with temperature zero. Effective reasoning remains unverified where the API does not report it.
- The initial UD-IQ4_XS SATA run used a 600-second case limit. Its paired 80k case timed out. Both paired 80k repeats subsequently completed with 900 seconds allowed; earlier successful rows were retained. The failed attempt, initial telemetry and extension sessions remain recorded. Subsequent storage conditions used 900 seconds without skipping remaining cases after timeout.
- Strata engine 0.1.52, the same model packages and a shared static Flash expert profile were used. Prior full copy verification and current size/completion-marker checks are recorded separately; weights were not rehashed during inference.
- Each pair was checked for equal **effective** expert placement. Automatic free-VRAM sizing initially differed. Explicit cache budgets or a supported native memory budget corrected that before measurement. Exact settings and rejected setup attempts are retained.

| Model | Verified GPU experts on both drives | Verified host placement | File tier / KV |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS | 2,343 cached; 5.27 GiB | 40 GiB locked; 0 GiB CUDA-pinned after pageable fallback | Unbuffered file tier; INT8 KV |
| Flash-Next IQ3_S | 3,116 cached; 5.97 GiB | 40 GiB locked; 0 GiB CUDA-pinned after pageable fallback | Through OS file cache; INT8 KV |
| Qwen3.6 UD-Q4_K_XL | 20 per layer; 1.46 GiB | All 18.75 GiB pinned; 1.10 GiB GPU staging | KV dtype unreported |

Qwen3.6 requested a 3.0 GiB expert budget on SATA and 2.60 GiB on NVMe to obtain the same 20-expert placement. Flash NVMe cache budgets were fixed to the SATA-selected counts. These temporary preset changes were restored after tests. OS standby caches were not forcibly flushed. Startup observations are not controlled cold-start measurements. Two repeats do not establish statistical significance or universal performance.

### Requested MTP versus observed drafting

MTP was requested and loaded for all three models. Native logs confirm draft attempts for both Flash variants on both drives. For Qwen3.6, **both conditions offered zero drafts** across 48 completed native request log rows each, including warmups. Its acceptance rate is undefined, rather than zero percent.

Inspection of the installed server identifies an inherited presence penalty of 1.5. The reviewed native Qwen source disables speculation with nonzero penalties, which explains the observed zero-draft path; source/binary equivalence was not independently established. Source hashes and this inference are retained in the JSON. A future penalty-neutral request would be a separate sampling condition; these measurements must not be relabeled as active Qwen MTP measurements. Flash counters can include suffix drafts and do not isolate MTP alone.

## Transfer measurements

All rates use decimal GB/s. Each 5070 Ti pass contains three timed samples per path; the table reports the median of three independent pass medians and their range. These captures preceded the inference storage experiment.

| Transfer path | RTX 5060 Ti reference | RTX 5070 Ti median | 5070 Ti pass range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Samsung 870 EVO SATA to RAM | 0.540 | 0.538 | 0.535–0.540 |
| AirDisk NVMe to RAM | 2.702 | 2.684 | 2.662–2.753 |
| Pinned RAM to VRAM | 6.582 | 13.434 | 13.410–13.435 |
| RAM copy, one worker | 9.929 | 8.530 | 8.466–8.533 |
| RAM copy, six workers | 20.634 | 22.011 | 21.299–22.164 |

The 5060 Ti reference uses its independent 02:57 UTC transfer capture, except NVMe, which uses its 11:05 UTC saved profile. The 5070 Ti captures are timestamped 19:16–19:18 UTC on 1 November 2026. RAM copy variation cannot be attributed to the GPU change alone.

Pinned host-to-device throughput is 2.04 times the 5060 Ti reference. A separate 15-sample diagnostic measured 13.409 GB/s and observed PCIe 3 x16 under transfer; idle observations included PCIe 1 x16. The 5060 Ti condition was PCIe 3 x8. Both used the i7-5820K platform, driver 617.42 and 64 GiB installed RAM.

Storage reads bypass the OS page cache using a flushed 256 MiB temporary file, 8 MiB blocks and queue depth one. Device caches can contribute. RAM copy counts copied payload, rather than total DRAM bus traffic. See [measurement methods](docs/measurements.md).

### Earlier 5060 Ti reference at 80k, one client

Both GPU records contain the same 312 historical workload keys across 13 models. The following comparison uses successful controlled-storage repeats, rather than the older 5070 Ti automatic-residency rows. Different expert counts, PCIe widths and measurement times prevent attribution to GPU compute alone; Qwen3.6 had 21 GPU experts per layer on the 5060 Ti and 20 here.

| Model / quant | SATA wall: 5060 → 5070 (s) | NVMe wall: 5060 → 5070 (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS | 324.16 → 329.12 | 177.77 → 163.04 |
| Flash-Next IQ3_S | 115.54 → 64.35 | 113.71 → 62.74 |
| Qwen3.6 35B A3B UD-Q4_K_XL | 188.58 → 94.71 | 189.92 → 92.92 |

See the [5060 Ti experiment](docs/5060-ti-storage-comparison.md) for its settings and censored 600-second paired workload.

## Memory, inventory and telemetry

Firmware reports four populated channels through explicit SMBIOS channel/slot labels, four 16 GiB DIMMs and a configured rate of 2133 MT/s. Active controller interleaving is **unverified** for this follow-up. A fresh [CPU-Z](https://www.cpuid.com/softwares/cpu-z.html) controller report was prepared, but Windows rejected normal execution with error 740, requiring administrator consent. The request remains pending. The older 5060 Ti CPU-Z quad-channel report remains historical evidence.

Storage detection confirms Samsung SSD 870 EVO 4TB on SATA and AirDisk 256GB SSD on NVMe. They are recorded in later inventory annotations and transfer snapshots, rather than retroactively asserted for every historical inference session. NVMe sequential reads were approximately 4.99 times the SATA rate.

OS-reported usable RAM differs by 4096 bytes from the original snapshot after reboot. Installed capacity, module count, clocks, CPU/core counts, board, OS and GPU/driver match. Transfer annotations retain this evidence without replacing the original hardware classification.

Whole-run telemetry retains CPU/GPU utilization, RAM/VRAM usage, GPU temperature and clock history, coverage and early/late summaries for all six conditions. Initial SATA timeout telemetry is retained separately from its continuation. Observed peak GPU temperature was 65°C; peak RAM usage was 96.3% during IQ3_S. CPU temperature was unavailable from the active collector. Samples include warmups and other applications; they do not establish thermal throttling or guaranteed sustained performance.

Strata Control owned every model lifecycle operation. All test models and its API were confirmed stopped afterward; desktop-only loading remains enabled.

## docs/pny-5070-ti-comparison.md

Canonical source: [docs/pny-5070-ti-comparison.md](docs/pny-5070-ti-comparison.md)

# PNY and ASUS Prime RTX 5070 Ti versus RTX 5060 Ti

The PNY card was measured once per case, using the same model set, six prompt targets and one/two clients as the reference cards. The PNY dataset contains **156 completed primary observations: 149 passed and 7 timed out**. The user cancelled the remaining storage follow-up; its partial observations and cancellation outcome are preserved separately and excluded from primary statistics. No completed PNY controlled SATA/NVMe comparison is claimed.

Across 76 comparable successful single-client primary cases, the median PNY/ASUS ratio was **1.023 for decode speed** and **1.073 for reported decode GPU watts**: about 2.3% faster decoding and 7.3% higher reported board power in this workload mix. Both cards reported a 300 W limit. These are medians of per-case ratios, rather than whole-run energy totals. One PNY repeat versus two ASUS repeats, unmeasured ambient conditions and board sensor differences limit conclusions about the designs.

[All model/context/client/card aggregates (CSV)](results/aggregates/pny-asus-5070-ti-5060-ti.csv) include actual token counts, prefill/decode, TTFT, board power, phase energy where available, whole-case energy for concurrent requests, temperatures, failure kinds and deadlines. Raw sessions and telemetry remain in the benchmark JSON files.

Prefill, decode and TTFT use the median over requests within each successful case, then the median over successful repeats. Min/max fields describe those case medians across repeats. PNY/reference ratios compare one PNY case with the reference median; known configuration conflicts suppress ratios and are listed in the CSV. Unreported backend settings remain unverified. Two-client whole-case energy is integrated once over the group, without summing overlapping request windows.

Each cell shows client prefill / decode in tokens/s, then measured decode GPU watts. Reference cells are medians of successful repeats. PNY has one observation. These cells do not establish statistical differences.

## Transfer measurements

GB/s uses decimal bytes. These short sequential/copy probes describe transfer paths, rather than model inference speed or DRAM controller bandwidth. PNY values below come from its fresh pre-benchmark capture; reference values retain their original capture provenance.

| Board | SATA read GB/s | NVMe read GB/s | Pinned RAM→VRAM GB/s | RAM copy, one worker GB/s | RAM copy, six workers GB/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTX 5060 Ti | 0.533 | 2.702 | 6.850 | 7.752 | 21.330 |
| ASUS Prime RTX 5070 Ti | 0.535 | 2.753 | 13.435 | 8.530 | 21.299 |
| PNY RTX 5070 Ti | 0.538 | 2.720 | 13.491 | 8.567 | 21.836 |

## Limits of the comparison

- GPU board watts and joules come from nvidia-smi. Whole-system watts and joules are estimates. No wall-meter measurement was made.
- Single-client phase energy is reported separately for prefill and decode. Two-client whole-case energy includes prefill, decoding and queueing; overlapping per-request windows are not summed.
- Prefill is prompt tokens divided by time to first visible token. Native Strata has one backend slot, so two-client values include queue delay.
- PNY primary LM Studio uses the current fixed 300-second deadline. Some ASUS LM Studio reference cases used older adaptive deadlines under a 1800-second configured cap. Successful ASUS LM Studio primary cases completed in less than 300 seconds, but censored outcomes must not be treated as speed ratios. Native primary uses 300 seconds; controlled storage uses 900 seconds.
- Primary ASUS/PNY Flash uses full locked/pinned RAM arenas, and primary Qwen3.6 uses 19 GPU experts per layer on both 5070 Ti boards. RTX 5060 Ti primary residency/placement differs, so its native comparison includes more than the GPU change. Completed controlled SATA/NVMe records in the CSV belong to the ASUS and 5060 Ti references; no PNY controlled pair was completed.
- Requested MTP does not prove that drafts were generated. Engine-scoped counters are retained; Flash counters can include suffix drafts. Qwen3.6 inherits the reference presence penalty, which can suppress drafting.
- OS standby caches were not forcibly flushed. Actual input/output token counts and per-case deadlines are retained. One PNY repeat limits conclusions about repeatability and small differences.
- Ambient temperature was not measured and cooling/fan behavior was not normalized. Temperature and power differences from this one-pass experiment cannot isolate board design alone.
- Board partner is user-identified; nonunique PCI subsystem/vBIOS observations distinguish the installed PNY board. Driver, CPU and memory provenance are recorded per session.

- [PNY RTX 5070 Ti](results/runs/20261102-004040_rtx-5070-ti_afd9bb57d2.json)

## docs/5960x-cpu-comparison.md

Canonical source: [docs/5960x-cpu-comparison.md](docs/5960x-cpu-comparison.md)

# PNY RTX 5070 Ti: i7-5820K versus i7-5960X

The same PNY RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB was measured with an i7-5820K 6c12t and an i7-5960X 8c16t. Driver 617.42, the 300 W GPU limit and 64 GiB memory configured at 2133 MT/s were retained. The 5960X dataset contains **156 recorded cases across the 13 established model variants: 149 successful and 7 unsuccessful/censored**. All 156 cases match the previous 5820K matrix. Each case has one repeat. The published cohort contains ten LM Studio variants and three Strata variants; Qwen3.6-35B is served by Strata, and the retained Qwen3.8-27B quant is Q3_K_XL.

[The complete 156-row case comparison CSV](results/aggregates/pny-5820k-vs-5960x.csv) includes both outcomes, actual token counts and context windows, quantization/mode/engine identity, configuration fingerprints, timings, measured GPU watts/joules, failures and ratio exclusions. Original per-source sessions and telemetry remain in the raw JSON.

These are descriptive comparisons from one pass on each CPU. Automatic worker choices, backend state, OS caching, clocks and ambient conditions were not independently controlled. Ratios require two successful cases and known compatible required metadata. Actual token counts are evaluated separately using the predeclared engineering tolerances below, rather than treated as model-configuration conflicts. Newly successful cases with a censored baseline have no invented baseline speed.

Ratios are 5960X/5820K, with an unweighted median across the eligible cells for that metric and client count. N is reported separately because the token/metric availability gates differ. Higher throughput and lower latency/energy ratios are favorable. These medians do not establish a statistical or causal CPU effect.

### Token-size matching rules

Old/new actual per-request token vectors are retained, sorted and compared element by element. Both vector lengths must equal the client count; missing usage is never replaced by the prompt target. The CSV exposes absolute deltas, maximum/median relative deltas, thresholds and per-metric eligibility/reasons. These tolerances are predeclared engineering choices for near-matched workloads, not statistical guarantees of equivalence.

- Prefill/decode tokens/s, decode GPU watts and normalized prefill/decode energy-per-token ratios require each input-token difference to be at most max(8 tokens, 2% of the larger count). Decode throughput uses the actually timed output-token numerator; a one-token input difference alone does not exclude it.
- Raw TTFT ratios use the tighter input rule max(4 tokens, 0.5% of the larger count).
- Raw whole-case wall-time and whole-case GPU-energy ratios require the 8-token/2% input rule and also the 8-token/2% rule for actual completion-token vectors. Whole-case GPU energy is available for concurrent groups, not a decode-only interval.
- Every metric additionally requires two successful cases, known compatible configuration and finite measured values with a positive baseline denominator. Failed/censored outcomes remain excluded even when partial token counts exist.

Values show client prefill / decode tokens/s and TTFT seconds. The CSV contains every prompt target and both client counts. Prefill is prompt tokens divided by client time to first observable output, including any queueing or unobserved reasoning; it is not an engine-only compute rate.

## Transfer paths

All rates below are decimal GB/s of copied payload. Logical read+write traffic is approximately twice RAM-copy payload; these probes do not measure memory-controller bus traffic. Four populated firmware channels do not independently verify active channel mode.

|Probe|5820K | 5960X|5960X/5820K|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|RAM copy, one worker|8.567|9.691|1.131|
|RAM copy, fixed six workers|21.836|23.399|1.072|
|RAM copy, automatic eight workers|Unavailable|21.933|Unavailable|
|Pinned RAM to VRAM|13.491|13.526|1.003|
|SATA sequential storage to RAM|0.538|0.538|1.000|
|NVMe sequential storage to RAM|2.720|2.816|1.035|

The matched six-worker measurement uses 64 MiB buffers per side per worker and eight copies per sample, matching the prior 21.8363 GB/s protocol. The 5960X fixed-six result is 23.3987 GB/s; automatic eight-worker 21.9327 GB/s is separate. Single-worker 9.691 versus 8.567 GB/s and pinned H2D 13.526 versus 13.491 GB/s describe these transfer paths. No controlled SATA/NVMe inference sweep was performed.

## First measured GPU compute and VRAM copy

These probes were first measured on the 5960X setup. There is no matching 5820K compute/VRAM probe, so they cannot show a CPU-related GPU throughput gain. Dense GEMM rates count multiplication and addition separately (2mnk), with 15 CUDA-event batch samples per shape and exact sampled-output validation. Tensor instruction selection was not independently profiled.

|Input / output arithmetic|Matrix edge|Median measured rate|
|---|---:|---:|
|FP32 SGEMM, pedantic/TF32 disabled|4096|35.68 TFLOP/s|
|FP32 SGEMM, pedantic/TF32 disabled|8192|36.63 TFLOP/s|
|FP16 inputs, FP32 compute requested/output|4096|100.33 TFLOP/s|
|FP16 inputs, FP32 compute requested/output|8192|101.77 TFLOP/s|
|INT8 inputs, INT32 accumulation/output|4096|330.03 TOPS|
|INT8 inputs, INT32 accumulation/output|8192|350.52 TOPS|

FP16 uses CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F and tensor-enabled math. Reduced-precision partial reductions were not explicitly disabled; strict FP32 accumulation throughout is unverified. INT8 uses TOPS, not TFLOP/s. INT4 is unavailable; quantized model weight bits do not establish hardware arithmetic precision.

|D2D payload|Payload GB/s|Nominal read+write GB/s|
|---:|---:|---:|
|256MiB|374.50|749.00|
|1024MiB|375.17|750.34|

Every copied destination byte passed a full SHA256 readback check. These are measured CUDA copy-path rates, not a theoretical DRAM peak. Separately, sustained unmeasured H2D activity observed PCIeGen3×16; this link-state observation does not replace the 13.526 GB/s matched H2D measurement. Raw clock/power/temperature samples and library/driver versions are embedded in the run.

## Native execution and energy scope

|Model|5820K CPU threads observed|5960X CPU threads observed|GPU experts, 5960X|Host residency evidence|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
|qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs|Unreported|Unreported|2469|55.44GiB full arena; pinned and VirtualLock evidence retained|
|qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s|Unreported|Unreported|3284|46.84GiB full arena; pinned and VirtualLock evidence retained|
|qwen3.6-35b-a3b-ud-q4_k_xl|6|8|19|Pinned hybrid-host memory observations retained|

- Native context remains 96K, with one backend slot queueing two clients. Effective expert cache/placement and actual locked/pinned host evidence are retained. Qwen automatic thread selection changing from six to eight is part of this configuration change; this is not a fixed-worker CPU microbenchmark.
- Actual KV dtype stays unknown where the backend does not report it. Qualified default-KV configuration equivalence is permitted only when explicit coordinator launch-capture sentinels document omitted --kv on both sides and known engine/version/context/effective expert cache match. This means the same backend-default configuration, not a verified dtype. Requested expert-VRAM budgets are retained as control settings; a budget adjustment alone does not conflict when actual expert placement and host residency agree.
- MTP requested does not prove drafts were generated. Engine-lifetime completion/draft counters include warmups; 30 completions are expected when all 12 cases succeed. Flash draft counters can include suffix drafts. Qwen retains the reference presence penalty, which can suppress drafting.
- Single-client prefill/decode GPU board watts and joules are measured by nvidia-smi. Two-client group GPU energy is integrated once across the whole case, including prefill, decoding and queueing. It is never labeled decode-only and overlapping request windows are not summed.
- Whole-system energy is an estimate, GPU + 60 W + 140 W×CPU-utilization fraction. The utilization denominator changes from 12 to 16 logical cores. Lower estimated system watts do not establish better measured CPU efficiency; no CPU package-energy or wall-meter measurement was made.
- Timeout/error outcomes remain in the CSV and raw data. A deadline is censoring, not a completed inference runtime. Failed/censored pairs have no speed/efficiency ratio.
- Repeats, ambient temperature, background activity, OS caches and automatic clocks limit precision. Small observed differences need further repeats. GPU compute/copy results are brief measured-throughput observations, not sustained inference predictions.

## PNY versus ASUS board comparison

The separate [PNY/ASUS/5060Ti report](docs/pny-5070-ti-comparison.md) found an approximately 2.3% higher median PNY decode rate and 7.3% higher measured decode GPU watts across 76 matched successful single-client cells. That comparison used one PNY repeat versus two ASUS repeats and is descriptive. It does not isolate board design from cooling, clocks or run-to-run variation.

## docs/5070-plus-5060-comparison.md

Canonical source: [docs/5070-plus-5060-comparison.md](docs/5070-plus-5060-comparison.md)

# Adding an ASUS RTX 5060 Ti to the PNY RTX 5070 Ti / i7-5960X

This setup contains a PNY RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB and ASUS RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB with the i7-5960X, 64 GiB memory, driver 617.42 and reported 300 W / 180 W board limits. **180 cases across 15 model variants** were recorded, one repeat per model/prompt/client cell. Outcomes: {"failed":1,"ok":179}. Both GPU boards are monitored individually and together.

[Full case comparisons](results/aggregates/5070-plus-5060-comparison.csv) · [Measurements across all five hardware configurations](results/aggregates/5070-plus-5060-all-configurations.csv) · [Shareable JSON](results/aggregates/5070-plus-5060-public.json)

**Measurement cohort complete:** all 144 LM Studio and 36 native Strata cells are included below, with one measured inference repeat per condition. Completed cells include recorded failures or censoring; completion of the grid does not mean every request succeeded.

## Main measured outcomes

- LM Studio: 120/120 matched cells completed, versus 113 successful baseline cells. Supplemental Qwen cells completed: 24/24.
- **LM Studio cohort only:** median matched single-client decode change -27.7% (57 eligible pairs); combined GPU decode J/token change +34.6% (57 pairs). Two-client per-request decode change -25.0% (55 pairs). These figures exclude native Strata rows.
- Native Strata: 35/36 successful attempts across 3 models; all 36 attempted, 1 timeout/censored deadline and 0 other unsuccessful outcomes. Its single-client matched decode change is -6.7% (12 eligible pairs), with per-model details and configuration qualifications below; native Qwen35 still selects one GPU.
- The supplemental LM Studio Qwen variants and native Strata variants remain separate engine/quantization conditions. Their practical rates appear below; no quality equivalence was measured.
- Gemma E2B has a severe LM Studio serving regression, confirmed by retained native server decode timings. Its cause remains unisolated by this cohort.
- A separate connection diagnostic found a roughly two-second IPv6/localhost fallback component. Client prefill/TTFT remain end-to-end measurements; no retrospective correction was applied.

## Comparison boundaries

The primary baseline is the same PNY RTX 5070 Ti and i7-5960X with one GPU. Adding the 5060 Ti and letting the runtime allocate work across both cards is the hardware/configuration treatment. The new pass also uses all-card telemetry; historical passes monitored the selected card. Request timing definitions are retained, but collector overhead was not independently isolated. Older 5060 Ti / ASUS 5070 Ti configurations also use the i7-5820K, so those are whole-system comparisons with a CPU difference. They are not isolated board-scaling experiments.

LM Studio follows its configured evenly distributed GPU strategy. Its strict VRAM cap is off; WDDM/shared-memory behavior is not separately measured, and dedicated VRAM readings alone do not establish fully resident placement. Strata Flash-Next supports layer splitting with the faster 5070 Ti as the main/output device; the native Qwen3.6 path supports a single selected GPU. Native execution observations appear below only for measured source runs. Per-engine launch observations and per-card VRAM/utilization identify actual behavior where reported. Merely installing two cards does not establish that each model executes across both.

Thirteen established variants form the matched cohort. The two supplemental user-tested LM Studio Qwen Q4_K_M variants address the larger combined capacity; they change engine and/or quantization relative to the single-card alternatives. No intelligence or quantization-quality conclusion follows from their speed.

N is the number of eligible workload cells, not an independent repeat count. Lower energy/token is favorable. Combined dual-card board energy is compared with single-card board energy, including the additional card’s idle consumption.

|qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs / UD-IQ4_XS|[1,0] / auto|1|5203|55.44 / full_arena_locked_or_pinned_within_log_rounding|4 / 4|3,556 / 2,046|True|

qwen3.6-35b-a3b-ud-q4_k_xl: GPU layer placement and effective expert-cache capacity are intended configuration treatments, not equality requirements; Actual KV dtype unreported in both native captures; matching engine defaults are qualified, not a verified dtype; Host expert allocation/residency evidence differs; native ratios require matching evidence. Configured max drafts are verified launch settings, not observed proposals or acceptance. Offered/accepted counters cover the loaded engine lifetime, including warmups; Flash counters may include suffix drafts as well as MTP. Zero offers means no speculative drafts were observed in those counters despite requesting MTP. Their full scope remains in the CSV; counts are not assigned to individual timed requests.

Expert-cache capacity and GPU layer placement change when the second card is available and are intended treatment effects. Their backend-specific counts are not interchangeable across FlashNext and Qwen35. Full FlashNext host arena evidence is separately required for eligible native ratios; pinned/locked residency does not establish that every unrelated process allocation is resident. Qwen35 uses its native single-GPU hybrid path; both boards remain inside measured power, including the unused card's draw. Two clients do not imply two native serving slots.

Transfers use decimal GB/s of copied payload. Each GPU path was probed separately; simultaneous combined host transfer and GPU-to-GPU bandwidth were not measured. The PCIe figures describe the installed card/path under load; they do not measure an empty slot or prove a different card’s negotiated width. The NVMe probe is a short uncached sequential-file read; device/controller caches can contribute. No controlled SATA/NVMe inference sweep was added. Four populated channels are inferred from firmware slot labels; active memory-controller mode remains unverified.

VRAM-copy rates count payload bytes; nominal read-plus-write traffic is about twice that figure. No simultaneous two-GPU compute or peer-transfer rate is inferred by summing these probes.

## Findings from the recorded cases

Across eligible matched cells, google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat has the highest median decode ratio, **1.028×** (9 cells), and google/gemma-4-e2b the lowest, **0.206×** (12 cells). These are descriptive model-specific observations from one pass.

|Single-card outcome|Dual-card outcome|Cells|
|---|---|---:|
|absent|ok|24|
|failed|ok|7|
|ok|failed|1|
|ok|ok|148|

Newly completed cells: google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat / 80,000 / 1 clients, google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat / 40,000 / 2 clients, google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat / 80,000 / 2 clients, lfm2.5-24b-a2b / 80,000 / 2 clients, qwen3.8-27b@q3_k_xl / 80,000 / 1 clients, qwen3.8-27b@q3_k_xl / 40,000 / 2 clients, qwen3.8-27b@q3_k_xl / 80,000 / 2 clients. No speedup is assigned against a failed baseline.

Previously successful cells that did not complete: qwen3.6-35b-a3b-ud-q4_k_xl / 80,000 / 2 clients. Raw failures and deadline evidence remain in the CSV.

LFM2.5 reasoning-only output was observed in **12/12** successful cases. The generation rate includes thinking tokens; a successful transport test is not proof of a completed visible task answer.

**Gemma E2B is a substantial regression, beyond the typical split-model loss.** At 20k its decode rate falls from 136.32 to 23.14 tokens/s; at 80k, from 110.32 to 7.85. The requests have matching context capacities, reported zero reasoning tokens and server-reported token counts. Retained LM Studio native timing lines independently report 23.15 and 7.85 decode tokens/s for those same requests. This confirms a serving-path slowdown rather than a missing-thinking-token numerator. During the 80k decode interval, observed dedicated VRAM peaks were only 4.08 / 4.19 GiB, average clocks were 2987 / 2798 MHz and temperature peaks were 57 / 52 °C for the 5070 / 5060. Those readings provide no evidence of dedicated-VRAM exhaustion or a large clock collapse. The exact cause requires separate profiling; this pass does not isolate cross-device attention/KV transfers or another backend implementation issue. No inference was repeated for this audit.


## Client connection overhead

A post-run, inference-free diagnostic measured median metadata-request latency of **2.062 s through localhost** versus **22.3 ms through IPv4 loopback**. Localhost resolved IPv6 first; direct IPv6 TCP attempts failed with Windows error 10061 after approximately two seconds, while IPv4 connected in about 15 ms. The running helper had no managed-base environment override and used the default localhost route. [Diagnostic samples](results/aggregates/5070-plus-5060-loopback-diagnostic.json) preserve the actual measurements.

This is evidence for a fixed connection component in client TTFT, especially visible on small prompts. LM Studio’s native prompt-evaluation timings are a different boundary: for the audited E2B 20k request they report 2.305 s of prompt evaluation versus 4.471 s client TTFT. The post-run probe used Python 3.12.15; inference used Python 3.13.14, so it is supporting connection-path evidence rather than a measured decomposition of every request.

The archived rates and energy remain unchanged. No fixed delay is subtracted, and historical helper environments are not reconstructed. Client prefill ratios should not be interpreted as isolated GPU prompt-evaluation ratios. For future profiles, explicitly selecting IPv4 loopback with LMS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1234 can avoid this observed fallback; collect fresh baselines or native server timings before mixing latency results across those connection profiles.


## Practical implications

Within the LM Studio cohort's measured automatic placement policy, adding the 5060 Ti has a median matched decode ratio of 0.729× and single-client decode energy/token ratio of 1.346×. For models and contexts that already fit the 5070 Ti, using that card alone is the better starting point for this measured throughput/energy trade-off. Assess native Strata separately because its placement and expert-cache policies differ.

The two-card setup has two separate VRAM pools. Automatic distribution is not equivalent to one GPU with twice the memory bandwidth. The 5060 Ti’s lower measured compute, VRAM-copy and host-transfer rates provide context for any scaling loss, but this experiment does not isolate their individual causal contributions.

For intuition, a sequential equal-work split between devices with relative rates 1 and 0.5 takes 0.5/1 + 0.5/0.5 = 1.5 time units, or about 0.67× the faster card’s rate, before communication overhead. This illustration assumes equal work and no overlap; actual model placement, batching and host experts can change that behavior.

Two simultaneous requests to one split model are not two independently placed model servers. A separate 5070-only / 5060-only serving experiment could test aggregate job throughput without splitting each request; it was not part of this matched pass.

## Measurement interpretation

- Prompt targets are 512, 5k, 10k, 20k, 40k and 80k, with one and two clients. The output budget is 256 tokens, matching the speed/watt reference; these are throughput tests, not capability tests.
- Prefill is actual prompt tokens divided by client TTFT. TTFT includes server scheduling, tokenization and queueing; it is not an isolated kernel rate. Concurrent request medians and aggregate output throughput are distinct metrics. Aggregate output is total reported completion tokens divided by whole-group wall time, including prefill.
- Configuration matching requires the same model, canonical quantization spelling, engine/version, reasoning/MTP request, context, sampling, corpus and protocol. Quantization labels are normalized only when reported; no quant is invented from a model ID. Native runtime draft counts, speculation threshold and quality-affecting controls must agree where either capture reports them. Historical declared drafts can be stale (3 versus actual4); runtime evidence takes precedence without altering raw history. GPU placement/effective cache changes are intended treatments, not matching failures. Full FlashNext host-arena residency is checked separately; omitted native KV/draft fields remain explicit qualifications, not invented values.
- Native Qwen35 host expert size and pinned/pageable allocation policy must match for eligible ratios. A pinned-to-pageable change is an explicit configuration difference; missing evidence is not treated as equality. Pageable allocation does not prove actual paging, shared-VRAM spill or disk traffic. Startup-only placement probes have no timed inference observations in this cohort.
- Throughput and normalized energy ratios require actual per-request input vectors within max(8 tokens, 2%). TTFT requires max(4 tokens, 0.5%). Whole-case time/energy and aggregate output rate additionally require completion vectors within max(8 tokens, 2%). Estimated completion counts are excluded from output-rate ratios. Both cases must succeed. All vectors, tolerances and exclusions are in the case CSV.
- Both GPU boards are sampled by nvidia-smi at a requested 150 ms interval. Combined phase energy requires complete power observations for both. Short or sparse windows are marked low confidence and excluded from energy-ratio summaries. Concurrent energy is integrated once over the whole group, never summed over overlapping requests.
- CPU utilization and system RAM are whole-client measurements. Per-card GPU load, VRAM, clocks, temperature and power are retained. Combined utilization is an unweighted device mean; it is not a compute-weighted saturation measure. The global VRAM peak comes from simultaneous sums, not the sum of independent card peaks.
- System power is an estimate: total GPU watts + 60 W + 140 W × CPU utilization fraction. No measured wall power or CPU package energy is available. Whole-run sampled energy includes loading and idle intervals and must not be labeled inference-only energy.
- Reasoning requested none is not proof of zero reasoning. Inspect first-output kind, actual reasoning-token counts and finish reasons. LFM2.5 can consume the full output budget in thinking; that records generation throughput, not a completed visible answer.
- A timeout is a censored outcome, not a completed 300-second inference. Failure counts and newly successful contexts are reported alongside speed, with no ratios against failures.
- One repeat, automatic clocks, ambient temperature, OS caches and unisolated background activity limit precision. This series describes practical configurations and does not establish statistical significance or a causal benefit from a particular board manufacturer.

See the [PNY/ASUS board report](docs/pny-5070-ti-comparison.md), [CPU comparison](docs/5960x-cpu-comparison.md), [storage follow-up](docs/5070-ti-hardware-follow-up.md) and [measurement definitions](docs/measurements.md) for their distinct protocols. Credentials, private paths and device UUIDs are excluded from public attachments.

---

## docs/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement.md

Canonical source: [docs/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement.md](docs/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement.md)

# Dual-GPU communication and placement investigation

This study records the PNY RTX 5070 Ti plus ASUS RTX 5060 Ti configuration.
For two RTX 5070 Ti cards, see the separate
[communication and placement comparison](docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md).

**Completed supplied diagnostic matrices.** These captures are separate from normal Wattever benchmark aggregates. Existing historical measurements remain unchanged.

Recorded conditions: 153 unprofiled screening and 3 profiled. Screening outcomes: {"allocation_failed":1,"failed":3,"ok":143,"unsupported_configuration":6}. Eligible timing conditions: 143. Required but absent case IDs: 0; unobserved required representative model/strategy/prompt/client combinations: 0. All entries in the supplied capture manifests were attempted. Full transfer capture available: True. Each measured inference condition has one repeat; internal CUDA-copy samples are not inference repeats.

The required150-condition screen is complete. Broad classic-row24 and fixed-output48 follow-up matrices were deferred under the user time limit; only the individually recorded closeout probes were attempted. Unattempted optional plan entries are deferred research, not pending attempted measurements or silently fabricated results.

[Raw shareable evidence (gzip JSON)](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-raw.json.gz) · [All conditions](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-conditions.csv) · [Matched strategy ratios](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-strategy-ratios.csv) · [Per-card telemetry](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-telemetry.csv) · [Original 180-case comparison](docs/5070-plus-5060-comparison.md)

## Communication topology and peer capability

Operator identities are PNY RTX5070 Ti16GB and ASUS RTX5060 Ti16GB; NVIDIA names and per-capture mappings verify logical ordering where provided. PnP endpoint/parent relationships are observed topology, while physical PE-slot labels remain unverified. Firmware generic Slot1–7 entries conflict with this three-slot board and are not used as slot proof.

|Observed endpoint|PnP Gen snapshot|Width snapshot|Parent bridge location|Physical slot|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti|3|16|PCI bus 0, device 3, function 0|unverified|
|NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti|3|8|PCI bus 0, device 2, function 0|unverified|
|Standard NVM Express Controller|3|4|PCI bus 0, device 1, function 0|unverified|

The [EVGA X99 Micro2 manual](https://www.evga.com/support/manuals/files/131-HE-E095_Part1_v2.pdf) documents x16/x16/x8 allocation with a40-lane processor, and the M.2/PE3 sharing rule. [Intel specifies40 PCIe3 lanes and four memory channels for5960X](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/products/sku/82930/intel-core-i75960x-processor-extreme-edition-20m-cache-up-to-3-50-ghz/specifications.html). These specifications do not prove which physical slots are occupied. Distinct observed root bridges do not establish absence of contention in host memory/controller paths; no active GPU lane loss is inferred from NVMe presence alone.

Negotiated link pairs during workload windows are retained in the telemetry CSV. Snapshot generation/width is not bandwidth; maxima of independent samples are not combined into an invented link state.

|Capture|Accessing CUDA device|Peer allocation device|Can access peer|
|---|---|---|---|
|0|0|1|False|
|0|1|0|False|
|1|0|1|False|
|1|1|0|False|

Unsupported peer access explicitly uses portable-pinned host staging. Peer-enabled CUDA API paths remain transport-unverified unless independently traced; capability or a peer-copy event alone is not labeled direct P2P.

## Transfer measurements

[Raw internal samples](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-micro-samples.csv) · [Transfer summaries](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-micro-summary.csv)

All rates below are medians of actual joint payload/elapsed samples. Simultaneous throughput is measured over a shared barrier-to-completion interval, never the sum of individual rates. Host latency includes Python dispatch, context/event handling and synchronization. Staged cross-device routes synchronize DtoH before HtoD; there is no within-route double-buffer pipeline. Host pages are CUDA-pinned with OS first-touch placement; CPU affinity/NUMA are not pinned. Full destination validation occurs after the last measured batch with prior poisoning, not independently after every internal sample. These short Windows/WDDM captures are not pure PCIe latency or peak VRAM bandwidth. Memory clocks were not captured, so no clock-state explanation is established. Requested mode names do not imply multiple copies: the actual copies-per-route field governs, including one copy at256MiB under the64MiB batch budget.
