A missing timed-window sample is unavailable evidence, not an idle link. Wrapper board energy covers allocations, warmups, validation and checkpoint I/O; it is not isolated transfer energy.

Its repeated random64KiB source block differs from the historical independent full-random pattern. Event and host rates count payload once; neither is a physical DRAM-controller traffic counter. Clock observations do not establish a boost/state cause.

These allocation-only samples are separate from copy samples and inference repeats.

|Capture|Sequence outcome|Held concurrently before cleanup GiB|Final release order|All host allocations released|Remaining allocations|Context destroyed|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|0|sequential allocations, each released before next|unavailable|per-attempt release|True|0|True|
|1|all_chunks_held_concurrently|18.75|reverse allocation order|True|0|True|

In the supplied fresh-context captures, single allocations of 16.00 GiB, 18.75 GiB failed despite passing the headroom gate. A pooled sequence held 18.75 GiB concurrently and completed verified cleanup. This demonstrates a working chunked allocation path; simple total-host-RAM exhaustion alone does not account for this contrast.


Pooled attempt status "held" describes ownership during the probe, before final cleanup. Per-chunk releases and the final global cleanup are reported separately above; a held-during-probe status is not an unreleased allocation. Capture-level held-byte totals are repeated as metadata in attempt rows and must not be added. If concurrent8+8+2.75GiB allocations succeed while a single16/18.75GiB allocation fails, chunking demonstrably helps in that fresh-context experiment and simple total-host-RAM exhaustion does not explain that contrast by itself. The native Runtime allocation in a loaded process remains a different API/context/state condition.

A fresh CUDA Driver context and cuMemHostAlloc flags0 are different API/context/state conditions from the native engine's Runtime allocation in a loaded process, even though flags0 correspond to the default allocation policy. Allocation success at a smaller size and CUDA out-of-memory at a larger size, despite OS headroom, measure those specific requests only. Buffers were not touched and no copies/kernels were run in this diagnostic. Exact failure cause and applicability to the native Qwen35 pageable-host condition remain unresolved; this does not prove that adding the second GPU caused the failure. Do not infer actual paging or a physical-RAM limit from that error alone.

## Controlled execution strategies

The baseline standalone matrix uses explicit IPv4 loopback, F16 requested K/V, reasoning off, MTP off, common weights, per-slot context and sampling. Optional cache-precision interventions are separate conditions, identified by requested and observed K/V types; the baseline F16 note does not apply to a q8 request. A nonbaseline precision is not claimed verified from a weight GGUF or an ignored flag: matching cache allocator evidence is required for its ratios/rankings. Unverified conditions retain actual timing observations in separate CSV columns/raw evidence. CPU offload, actual layer placement and native tensor restrictions remain recorded outcomes. Automatic fitting may choose different weight placement; no tensor-mode fallback is silently substituted. Independent instances use one logical model instance per card; file-backed GGUF pages may be shared by the OS, so this does not establish twice the physical host RAM. One-client independent runs still pay the second loaded card's idle draw. Do not sum process RSS or per-card shared allocations as physical RAM; OS total-minus-available is the global physical-memory boundary. Tensor restrictions belong to the actual pinned architecture/build, not a generic promise of support.


[Final-load allocation evidence](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-actual-placement.csv) isolates the last model-loader pass with positive real model buffers, excluding earlier dry fit passes and zero-size allocations. KV allocations are read from the last positive KV context when context markers establish it. Unavailable pass/context boundaries and startup-prefix truncation remain explicit; no dry CPU KV/layer assignment is silently combined with a final GPU allocation.

An offloaded41/41 layer message does not establish that all weights reside in GPU memory: tensor/expert overrides can retain nonzero CPU_Mapped model allocations. The original offload flags remain reported metadata, alongside final positive CPU/host/GPU model-buffer sizes. CPU embeddings/output tensors and explicitly named expert policies are identified separately; a host buffer with no tensor-role evidence is not labeled an expert by its size. Logged allocation sums are not independent physical-RAM totals, active compute placement, or a per-layer KV map.


The frozen runner warms each engine with only8 generated tokens. This does not establish that every CPU-offloaded memory-mapped GGUF page or rarely used MoE expert was prefaulted, nor that filesystem-cache state was equal across conditions. GPU startup loading and an8-token warmup do not verify full host-weight residency. First-query file-backed demand paging can cause page reads without RAM exhaustion or pagefile swapping. Per-phase reads, process working set and faults provide qualified context only; global counters include other processes, and no SSD bottleneck is claimed without attributed I/O evidence. Filesystem/host-page state is separate from token-prefix cache reuse: cache_prompt=false and a zero reused-token count do not prove a cold or equal OS file cache.


In this new strategy matrix, single5070 and single5060 mean execution on one GPU while the other card remains physically installed and idle. Their all-card energy includes that idle board. Historical physically single-card installations have a different energy boundary and remain separate; these labels never mean the other board was removed.

Classic `row` is a separate placement strategy from experimental `tensor`: the row adapter requests a weight partition across both cards while keeping KV/intermediates on the designated main GPU; experimental tensor mode shards KV and performs cross-device reductions. These are requested policies, not proof of actual placement. Wrapper SHA256/strategy definitions remain in the conditions/raw evidence; unchanged core measurement/client/power source fingerprints are still required for matched strategy comparisons.

[Pinned llama.cpp CUDA documentation](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/3f8af15a7/docs/multi-gpu.md). Per-model unsupported cases are retained above and in the conditions CSV. Failed/censored runs have no fabricated zero throughput.

Matched ratios require identical software/weight-header identity, requested parameters, context, prompt hashes and actual input counts. Full-file hashes are reported when available; a header/tensor-directory hash is not proof of every weight byte. Strict decode, whole-group throughput/elapsed and energy ratios additionally match actual output counts; TTFT/prefill comparisons do not require matching future output length. Early EOS is allowed: a common output budget does not force identical completion counts. Separate descriptive same-budget ratio columns retain valid actual-work comparisons when counts differ, with both counts and the length qualification; they are not pooled into strict ratios. Absolute tokens/s remains available for every verified successful condition. Requested KV flags and observed raw placement logs remain separate evidence; a split fraction is not an actual weight/KV map.

Ratios are strategy/single5070 within the new controlled protocol. They do not pool native Strata, LM Studio, smoke or profiled measurements. Backend prompt-evaluation durations are retained separately and may be unassigned to requests; they are not substituted for client TTFT.

## Why prefill can improve while decode slows

[Bounded startup pipeline evidence](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-pipeline-startup.csv) retains startup enabled/disabled messages and n_copies, but reported active settings require the independently isolated final real positive KV-context epoch. Earlier fit/dry-run pipeline messages are retained separately and do not establish the active setting. The split request alone never establishes that pipelining was enabled. Missing messages, unisolated contexts, truncated startup coverage and mixed states remain explicit; a logged pipeline setting alone does not establish overlapping GPU kernels or a phase-specific speedup.

|qwen35|independent|80000|1|server0|screening|unavailable|unreported|[]|Final real positive KV context|True|
|qwen35|independent|80000|1|server1|screening|unavailable|unreported|[]|Final real positive KV context|True|
|qwen35|independent|80000|2|server0|screening|unavailable|unreported|[]|Final real positive KV context|True|
|qwen35|independent|80000|2|server1|screening|unavailable|unreported|[]|Final real positive KV context|True|

A plausible execution explanation is that prefill has many prompt tokens and microbatches available for pipelining, while a single autoregressive decode stream must complete each token through its dependent layers before the next token. Actual pipeline startup messages and recorded GPU overlap support only the observed parts of that explanation; whole-request traces without a verified phase clock cannot isolate prefill concurrency. Two clients are a separate workload and can change scheduling.
Heterogeneous execution can also slow decode without PCIe being the dominant cost: serial layer work assigned to the slower card can lengthen the critical path, through its weight/KV reads and kernels. As an illustrative calculation only, half the weights scanned at bandwidth B and half at B/2 would take1.5 times a full scan at B, ignoring every other cost. This is not a measured model DRAM rate or a prediction from the local-copy reference. Requested split fractions need not equal actual weight bytes or computation. Measured transfer/wait evidence, actual placement, CPU/offload and quantized-KV conditions are considered separately; PCIe capability alone does not establish causality.

## Gemma E2B: measured regression and current hypothesis

The preceding report independently confirmed severe20k/80k decode regressions in native server timing logs; the localhost fallback affects TTFT and cannot by itself explain post-first-token decode rates. Existing low dedicated VRAM and high clocks did not establish a paging diagnosis.

Pinned [Gemma source](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/3f8af15a7/src/models/gemma4.cpp) and the inspected GGUF identify35 layers with20 shared-KV tail layers, using zero-based source layers13 and14. A split that separates those sources from tail15–34 could cause repeated context-dependent cross-device reads/copies. Reverse CUDA device order1,0 with fractions1,2 is a proposed placement experiment, not proof of causality. Weight-colocation flags are accepted only for unsplit/layer modes with nonsharded CUDA model-buffer evidence; row/tensor main-device assignments do not establish whole weight-layer colocation. Actual KV allocation/reuse and transfer/wait causality require KV logs and traces.

## Profiling and counter availability

[Sanitized trace summaries](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-profiles.csv)

Nsight captures exclude model loading by starting collection after readiness/warmup, but injection is present before collection. Graph-node tracing and diagnostic logging/sampling add unquantified overhead. Profiled points are excluded from timing/energy rankings. CPU stack/context-switch capture, WDDM event tracing and GPU hardware counters are not enabled by the helper; no privilege/driver/global-trace changes were made. Missing trace/counter evidence remains unavailable, never measured zero.


[Profile/unprofiled allocation comparison](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-profile-placement-comparison.csv) checks matching model-file/runtime identities, GPU mapping, requested strategy/context and K/V precision using the separately parsed final real allocations. Nsight injection before model loading can consume VRAM and perturb --fit decisions, including CPU expert placement. A trace therefore does not establish the unprofiled run's weight/KV placement. Differences are flagged without normalizing timing; missing or truncated allocation evidence remains unavailable. Output-stop/budget differences are identified and any placement comparison across them remains qualified. Even equal aggregate buffer sizes do not prove identical tensor placement.

|Model|Strategy|Prompt|Trace status / analysis|GPU event counts|Logical requested copy bytes|Sum wait API ns|Event-time sanity flags|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|gemmae2b|single5070|20000|analyzed / enum_corrected_sidecar|{"kernel":282688,"memcpy":4712,"runtime":86741}|1857839088|1497171270|0|
|gemmae2b|layer_equal|20000|analyzed / enum_corrected_sidecar|{"kernel":283975,"memcpy":36127,"runtime":156715}|102802640324|10576803614|2|
|gemmae2b|gemma_kv_local|20000|analyzed / enum_corrected_sidecar|{"kernel":220644,"memcpy":16023,"runtime":114013}|3441544540|1980665276|0|

Memory-kind and copy-direction labels follow each captured SQLite export's enum tables. Validated sidecars must retain capture-source/SQLite provenance and unchanged counts, logical bytes and timing; originals remain archived. Legacy archived label strings are unverified and are not used as evidence of placement. Missing enum tables produce unknown labels rather than an assumed ordering.

Trace memcpy bytes are logical requested-copy sizes, not independently measured physical PCIe traffic. Requested bytes divided by summed event durations can exceed the platform's physical PCIe ceiling because graph/replay semantics, event timing and overlap differ from hardware bus accounting. The event-time sanity flags identify such inconsistencies; they are not throughput measurements. CPU wait/API and copy durations overlap and cannot be added as elapsed bus time or idle time. Actual phase NVML KB/s samples, when available, remain separate evidence.

[Client-boundary telemetry timeline](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-client-phase-timeline.csv) uses the recorded request start/first-output/end and sampler perf_counter timestamps. It can assign NVML/WDDM/CPU observations to client TTFT and decode windows, with counter sampling windows possibly straddling a boundary. This is not a native kernel-prefill definition. The Nsight traces remain whole-request collections: no verified clock transform to those client phases is available, and no per-phase kernel/copy causality is claimed from an inferred offset or a backend duration. Corresponding phase figures contain no guessed Nsight overlay.


Trace-local GPU activity unions avoid double counting overlapping kernel/copy intervals. API-duration sums can overlap and are not elapsed idle time. Gaps mean no recorded GPU activity, not proven hardware idle. NVML PCIe counters retain raw driver KB/s and sampling windows; they are not integrated transfer bytes. WDDM shared allocation is not proof of spill; global paging includes unrelated applications, process faults include soft/hard faults, and commit charge is not actual pagefile occupancy.

Both board powers, energy, utilization, VRAM, clocks and temperatures are retained per condition/card. Group energy is integrated once over the common overlapping-job window. Energy rankings require complete inventory and power on both unique cards, no low-confidence or truncated-retention flag, and at least80% sampled temporal coverage globally and per card. The sampler extrapolates time-weighted sampled power to window edges; accepted energy is not proof of continuous physical measurement. Coverage and eligibility exclusions remain explicit in conditions CSV. Decode-phase energy uses its own verified interval and coverage. Do not add per-request energies or independent VRAM peaks; the combined VRAM peak is the maximum simultaneous sum. CPU/wall-system energy is not measured. Per-process CPU/memory, global paging, collection overhead and counter availability remain in the telemetry attachment/raw evidence.

[Failed-attempt sensors](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-failed-attempt-telemetry.csv) retain whole-sampler-interval diagnostics when a timeout/failure leaves the request group empty. This is not a reconstructed aligned group window: no throughput, group-energy/token or capacity-OOM conclusion is fabricated from a timeout. Raw sensor samples remain in the separate failed-capture evidence.

## Recommendations within tested conditions

The following are best observed points among matched, successful, unprofiled configurations. One repeat cannot establish statistical significance, stability across ambient conditions, or model intelligence. Recommendations remain specific to model, context, client count and measured GPU-board boundary.

## Historical comparisons and connection boundary

See the [180-case dual-card comparison](docs/5070-plus-5060-comparison.md), [CPU comparison](docs/5960x-cpu-comparison.md), and [single-card hardware follow-up](docs/5070-ti-hardware-follow-up.md). They retain original weights, KV/MTP/reasoning flags, endpoint paths, power boundaries and timestamps. New controlled F16-KV/MTP-off standalone results are a separate condition; native Strata variants and LM Studio variants are not merged into its ratios.

The retained inference-free localhost diagnostic found a roughly two-second IPv6 fallback versus direct IPv4. New controlled requests explicitly use127.0.0.1 with proxy bypass. Historical client TTFT/prefill rates are unchanged; no guessed delay is subtracted. Native prompt-evaluation timing remains a separate boundary. Decode regressions supported by native post-first-token timing require another explanation.

[Retained historical context rows](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-historical-context.csv) are copied read-only from the existing aggregate CSV. The20k/80k single-client observations below are context, not matched new-strategy ratios. Different quants/engines, CPU configurations, repeats and energy boundaries remain identified.

## Reproduction and evidence limits

```powershell
$benchPython = "C:\tests\flash-next\.venv\Scripts\python.exe"
& $benchPython untracked/run_communication_capture.py --smoke
& $benchPython untracked/run_communication_capture.py
& $benchPython tools/standalone_screen.py --run --models gemmae2b --sizes 512 20000 80000 --clients 1 2 --stop-after 1 --output untracked/communication-investigation/screening-gemma
# Inspect the first newly measured condition, then retain the full plan and resume once:
& $benchPython tools/standalone_screen.py --run --models gemmae2b --sizes 512 20000 80000 --clients 1 2 --resume --output untracked/communication-investigation/screening-gemma
& $benchPython tools/standalone_screen.py --run --models lfm25 qwen27 qwen35 --sizes 512 20000 80000 --clients 1 2 --output untracked/communication-investigation/screening-remaining
# Profiling adds --profile --nsys <pinned-x64-nsys.exe> and uses a NEW diagnostic directory.
# Reporting uses default Python with matplotlib/numpy; the FLASH venv owns GPU measurements.
python untracked/report_communication_investigation.py --generate
```

Commands describe the protocol, not blanket permission to interrupt active services. Before GPU work the harness requires prior cohort completion, fresh Strata state and no loaded LM Studio/standalone model; native Strata lifecycle remains owned by Strata Control. Bind only verified-free ports and stop only verified owned processes. Exact condition parameters, actual executable versions/hash, model/header identity and software provenance are in raw evidence.

The archived study runners encode this Windows machine's guarded layout and model inventory; they are research sources, not a claim of a universally portable launcher. Other machines can use stock llama.cpp with the recorded parameters and Wattever's ordinary OpenAI-compatible endpoint workflow, recording their own actual placement and hardware metadata.

**Measured:** validated copy samples, saved successful inference timing/usage and available sensors. **Inferred:** documented lane-allocation implications and the possible Gemma shared-KV cross-split mechanism. **Unresolved unless supplied traces/logs establish it:** physical slot assignment, direct peer transport, per-layer KV placement, paging attribution, and whether transfer/waiting causally accounts for the decode loss. CPU/memory/PCIe capacity alone is not a causal diagnosis.


## Background activity and uncertainty

[Measurement qualification](results/aggregates/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement-operational-events.json) retains nonconfidential background-activity information. Historical inputs are verified against their original size/SHA256; any relocated input must match its explicit authorized mapping and the same original checksum.

A brief background read was recorded during the independent-instance phase; exact timing and the specific overlapping case are unknown. No effect size was established and no retrospective timing correction was applied. Per-case telemetry is retained. Small differences remain descriptive observations under a one-repeat design, without a statistical-significance claim.

## Targeted closeout evidence

The successful Qwen27B80k closeout explicitly logs final real K(q8_0)/V(q8_0), with CPU KV352.75MiB and CUDA0 KV2469.25MiB. Its observed5.283 decode tokens/s and639.56 client prefill tokens/s remain a separate Q8 cache condition with actual80496 input and223 output tokens; they are not pooled into F16 rankings or exact-output comparisons. This is one successfully observed context, not a maximum-capacity estimate.

The fixed256 Gemma single5070 anchor completed with hash-bound effective ignore_eos verification. The classic-row comparison failed during model loading because the pinned backend reported that CUDA0 does not support split buffers; no row-mode inference measurement exists for that condition. This is distinct from the earlier experimental tensor graph split-axis assertion.

## docs/two-5070-ti-comparison.md

Canonical source: [docs/two-5070-ti-comparison.md](docs/two-5070-ti-comparison.md)

# Two RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB cards: performance, energy and temperature

This benchmark compares a PNY RTX 5070 Ti plus an ASUS Prime RTX 5070 Ti with
the same PNY card alone and with a PNY RTX 5070 Ti plus ASUS RTX 5060 Ti. All
three configurations use an Intel Core i7-5960X and 64 GiB of RAM. The two-5070
configuration records **180 cases: 179 successful and one timeout**, with one
measured inference repeat per condition.

Native Strata Flash-Next IQ3_S showed higher observed throughput on two 5070 Ti
cards. Most LM Studio models had decode rates closer to the single-card rates,
while Gemma E2B retained a large regression. These are comparisons of complete
observed configurations: endpoint transport, automatic placement and host-memory
registration also affect their interpretation.

[Two-card raw measurements](results/runs/20261103-100532_rtx-5070-ti_0a91ddc850.json)
· [Single-PNY baseline](results/runs/20261102-041639_rtx-5070-ti_6b6060174b.json)
· [Mixed-card baseline](results/runs/20261102-175334_rtx-5070-ti_9116ad932f.json)
· [Every paired case and eligibility gate](results/aggregates/two-5070-ti-paired-cases.csv)
· [Per-model summaries](results/aggregates/two-5070-ti-model-summary.csv)
· [Absolute case measurements](results/aggregates/two-5070-ti-absolute-cases.csv)

## Hardware and protocol

| Setting | Recorded condition |
|---|---|
| CPU and memory | Intel Core i7-5960X, 8 cores / 16 threads, 64 GiB RAM |
| GPU0 / GPU1 | PNY RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB / ASUS Prime RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB |
| GPU driver | NVIDIA 617.42 |
| Backend versions | LM Studio 0.4.24+1; native Strata engine 0.1.52 |
| Prompt targets | 512, 5k, 10k, 20k, 40k and 80k tokens |
| Simultaneous clients | One and two |
| Generation settings | 256-token maximum output budget, temperature 0, requested reasoning none |
| Inference repeats | One per model / target / client-count condition |
| Case deadline | 300 seconds |
| Outcome | 179 successful; native Qwen35 at 80k / two clients timed out |

The 15 model variants comprise **144 LM Studio and 36 native Strata cases**.
Against the single-PNY baseline, **13 shared model IDs cover 156 common
model/target/client cells**. Two additional LM Studio Qwen Q4_K_M variants
contribute 24 supplemental cells. They remain separate from native Strata and
other-quantization variants. The mixed-card baseline contains all 15 variants.

The final native Qwen35 cases were measured in a separate session after a reboot.
Two partial LM Studio attempts from monitoring interruptions remain archived
outside the 180 primary observations. Successful observations were preserved;
the final native timeout was recorded without a retry.

LM Studio uses its recorded managed context and allocation settings. Native
Strata uses a 98,304-token context and one serving slot; submitting two clients
therefore includes queueing at that server. Two installed cards do not establish
that a backend executes across both. Runtime evidence below distinguishes them.

## How to interpret the measurements

### Hardware probe references

The normal JSON also retains fresh hardware probes, outside inference timing.
Four 16 GiB DIMMs report A1/B1/C1/D1 placement at 2133 MT/s: four populated
firmware channels are inferred; active controller mode is not independently
verified. Native RAM-copy throughput counts copied payload once, not physical
DRAM bus traffic.

| Probe | Observed result |
|---|---:|
| Single-worker native RAM copy | 8.30 GB/s |
| Eight-worker native RAM copy | 22.86 GB/s |
| Matched six-worker native RAM copy | 23.41 GB/s |
| Samsung 870 EVO sequential read, queue depth 1, OS cache bypassed | 0.539 GB/s |
| Pinned RAM to PNY / ASUS GPU, fresh automatic probe | 13.51 / 13.56 GB/s |

That storage reading measures the SATA probe volume, not the separate NVMe.
The [communication study](docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md) retains later transfer
controls with a distinct protocol and verifies both loaded GPU links at Gen3 x16.

At 8192-square dense GEMM, the measured medians below use CUDA-event batches,
five warmups and 15 internal samples with analytical readback checks. They are
observed arithmetic throughput, not advertised peak specifications or inference
predictions. The actual library algorithm is retained; its instruction path was
not independently profiled.

| Arithmetic | PNY 5070 Ti | ASUS Prime 5070 Ti |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP32, TF32 disabled | 36.41 TFLOP/s | 36.25 TFLOP/s |
| FP16-input GEMM | 101.15 TFLOP/s | 96.57 TFLOP/s |
| INT8-input GEMM | 347.97 TOPS | 346.63 TOPS |

Integer throughput uses TOPS. No INT4 arithmetic measurement was made, and
GGUF weight bit-width is not the precision of every inference operation.

### Timing, matching and energy boundaries

**Client prefill is actual prompt tokens divided by client-observed TTFT.** It
includes transport, queueing and other work before observable output. Backend
prompt-evaluation counters, where available, remain separate. See the
[measurement definitions](docs/measurements.md).

Managed LM Studio requests in the two-5070 pass use explicit IPv4; the historical
normal baselines used `localhost`. A separate metadata-GET diagnostic observed
approximately 2.06 seconds through `localhost` versus 22 milliseconds through
IPv4. That does not measure a fixed chat-request delay. Historical timings are
unchanged, and no guessed delay is subtracted. **LM Studio prefill and TTFT
changes cannot be attributed wholly to the extra GPU.** Native Strata used IPv4
in both cohorts.

Ratios below are unweighted medians of eligible per-case ratios. Each metric has
its own eligible-pair count, **N**; N counts workload cells, not independent
repeats. Input/output proximity gates allow up to the larger of eight tokens or
2%; TTFT input gates allow four tokens or 0.5%. Whole-case comparisons also
require output-count proximity. The CSVs retain a separate strict exact-count
subset. Equal counts do not prove equal generated text or token sequences.

GPU energy covers both installed boards, including an idle secondary card.
Concurrent case energy is integrated once over the shared group interval; it
is not the sum of overlapping request energies. Decode J/token covers the
observed generation interval after first output, whereas whole-case energy
includes the group's prompt and generation work.
CPU/system power is estimated, not measured at a wall socket. Historical
physically single-card energy keeps its original one-board boundary.

## Matched performance and energy

Each cell reports median percentage change and eligible N. Positive throughput
and negative energy changes are favorable. LM Studio and native Strata remain
separate cohorts.

| Reference | Backend | Clients | Client prefill change (N) | Decode change (N) | Decode GPU J/token change (N) | Whole-case GPU energy change (N) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Single PNY 5070 Ti | LM Studio | 1 | +108.4% (57) | −5.1% (57) | +31.4% (40) | Unavailable (0) |
| Single PNY 5070 Ti | LM Studio | 2 | +91.1% (55) | −2.8% (55) | Unavailable (0) | +11.0% (27) |
| Single PNY 5070 Ti | Native Strata | 1 | +7.9% (12) | +45.6% (12) | +15.4% (12) | Unavailable (0) |
| Single PNY 5070 Ti | Native Strata | 2 | +19.0% (12) | +67.3% (12) | Unavailable (0) | +30.0% (6) |
| 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti | LM Studio | 1 | +106.2% (72) | +29.3% (72) | +0.2% (53) | Unavailable (0) |
| 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti | LM Studio | 2 | +79.7% (72) | +28.4% (72) | Unavailable (0) | −7.3% (40) |
| 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti | Native Strata | 1 | +9.1% (18) | +21.8% (18) | +9.1% (18) | Unavailable (0) |
| 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti | Native Strata | 2 | +13.3% (17) | +50.3% (17) | Unavailable (0) | +7.5% (9) |

Native Strata versus the single-PNY baseline includes the two Flash-Next
variants. Native Qwen35 is excluded because its host allocation differs, as
explained below. The mixed-card native comparison includes Qwen35 where both
conditions have compatible evidence. These different eligible populations are
not interchangeable.

### Native Flash-Next by quantization

These single-client medians span the six prompt targets. Registration policy
and expert-cache placement are part of the observed configuration treatment.

| Quantization | Reference | Client prefill change (N) | Decode change (N) | GPU decode J/token change (N) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| IQ3_S | Single PNY 5070 Ti | +24.9% (6) | +74.8% (6) | −7.2% (6) |
| UD-IQ4_XS | Single PNY 5070 Ti | +5.4% (6) | +23.5% (6) | +31.4% (6) |
| IQ3_S | 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti | +12.6% (6) | +83.5% (6) | −22.6% (6) |
| UD-IQ4_XS | 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti | +34.5% (6) | +21.8% (6) | +16.4% (6) |

## Absolute single-client throughput

Values are **client prefill / decode, in tokens per second**. Prompt lengths
label target groups; actual token counts and output lengths are retained in the
raw measurements. Each row is a separate engine/quantization condition.

| Model / quantization | Backend | 20k target | 80k target |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Gemma 4 12B QAT / Q4_0 | LM Studio | 5,258.79 / 73.90 | 3,934.48 / 66.42 |
| Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT / Q4_0 | LM Studio | 5,738.35 / 116.68 | 4,885.77 / 99.67 |
| Gemma 4 E2B / Q4_K_M | LM Studio | 8,801.83 / 29.90 | 5,456.91 / 10.08 |
| Gemma 4 E4B / Q4_K_M | LM Studio | 7,348.75 / 82.22 | 5,913.20 / 66.06 |
| LFM2.5-24B-A2B / Q4_0, QAD | LM Studio | 8,034.16 / 175.28 | 7,228.24 / 128.68 |
| GPT-OSS-20B / MXFP4 | LM Studio | 8,077.44 / 124.58 | 5,735.17 / 100.77 |
| Bonsai-27B / Q1_0 | LM Studio | 3,168.79 / 71.26 | 2,157.14 / 51.72 |
| Qwen3.5-9B / Q4_K_M | LM Studio | 7,316.71 / 82.08 | 5,356.02 / 64.41 |
| Qwen3.8-27B / Q3_K_XL, UD | LM Studio | 2,795.28 / 41.60 | 1,976.39 / 33.77 |
| Spark-X2.6-4B / Q4_K_M | LM Studio | 8,956.42 / 115.06 | 6,166.78 / 83.05 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B / Q4_K_M | LM Studio, supplemental | 5,797.96 / 130.13 | 4,902.14 / 105.96 |
| Qwen3.8-27B / Q4_K_M | LM Studio, supplemental | 2,810.55 / 37.76 | 1,977.97 / 31.51 |
| Flash-Next / UD-IQ4_XS | Native Strata | 1,062.01 / 18.18 | 1,971.69 / 17.55 |
| Flash-Next / IQ3_S | Native Strata | 1,089.00 / 73.26 | 2,359.37 / 69.58 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B / UD-Q4_K_XL | Native Strata | 493.06 / 33.09 | 460.58 / 11.59 |

For example, the native IQ3_S 80k case used 80,996 prompt tokens and generated
195 tokens. The UD-IQ4_XS case used 81,008 / 196; native Qwen35 used 80,999 / 229.
These stopping lengths differ. Speed does not establish model-quality or
quantization-quality equivalence.

Gemma E2B's LM Studio single-client decode median was 72.9% below the
single-PNY baseline across six eligible cells. The normal cohort establishes
the observed regression; communication and placement causality require the
separate diagnostic study.

## Native execution and speculative decoding

Qwen's model card distinguishes a **125B language model with 6B activated**,
plus **51B n-gram embeddings and a 4B MTP component**. Approximately 180B across
those components is different from the activated language-model count; quant
file size is not a parameter-count measurement. [Publisher model overview](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next/raw/main/README.md).

| Model / quantization | Selected GPUs | Serving slots | Expert memory evidence | Draft configuration | Observed offered / accepted |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Flash-Next / UD-IQ4_XS | GPU1 then GPU0 | 1 | 55.44 GiB resident arena; 5,311 GPU-cached experts | Four drafts requested | 3,569 / 2,019 |
| Flash-Next / IQ3_S | GPU1 then GPU0 | 1 | 46.84 GiB resident arena; 7,196 GPU-cached experts | Four drafts requested | 3,426 / 2,027 |
| Qwen3.6-35B / UD-Q4_K_XL | GPU0 only | 1 | 18.75 GiB pageable host experts; 19 per layer cached on GPU | MTP requested; head loaded | 0 / 0 |

The draft counters cover each loaded engine's lifetime, including warmups;
they are not per-case acceptance measurements. GPU order does not by itself
verify every tensor or KV-cache placement. Flash-Next records INT8 KV and a
96k allocation. Native Qwen35's actual KV dtype is unreported.

Native Qwen35 executes on **one GPU** despite two installed cards. Its
single-PNY baseline reported pinned host experts, while this pass used pageable
host experts. Those single-to-dual ratios are excluded (N=0). Against the
pageable mixed-card condition, six single-client and five two-client cells are
eligible. Pageable allocation alone is not evidence of pagefile traffic.

## Resident RAM is not the same as CUDA registration

Startup logs account for resident Flash expert arenas using a combination of
CUDA-registered slices and Windows VirtualLock. VirtualLock keeps pages resident
but does not register those pages with CUDA. Reported CUDA-registered GiB below
are **integer floors**, not exact byte counts.

| Quant / arena | Setup | VirtualLock MiB | Registered slices | Registered GiB floor |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| UD-IQ4_XS / 55.44 GiB | Single PNY 5070 Ti | 27,365 | 25 | 28 |
| UD-IQ4_XS / 55.44 GiB | 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti | 48,978 | 6 | 7 |
| UD-IQ4_XS / 55.44 GiB | Two 5070 Ti | 48,978 | 6 | 7 |
| IQ3_S / 46.84 GiB | Single PNY 5070 Ti | 17,977 | 31 | 29 |
| IQ3_S / 46.84 GiB | 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti | 40,290 | 8 | 7 |
| IQ3_S / 46.84 GiB | Two 5070 Ti | 40,290 | 8 | 7 |

Both dual-card captures log the engine's 8 GiB registration cap for multi-GPU
Windows/WDDM execution. The version-pinned upstream documentation describes a
pinned staging ring for the remainder. This is an engine policy rather than a
universal hardware limit. The exposed registration override was not tested in
this study. [Strata 0.1.52 source documentation](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/a42cc3d7df70/docs/MULTI_GPU.md#L133-L138).

Single-to-dual native comparisons change registration composition alongside
GPU/cache placement. Their performance differences are complete-configuration
outcomes, not isolated GPU-compute or DMA effects. For each quant, the
mixed-card and two-5070 captures have identical reported pin/lock composition;
that difference does not distinguish those two dual-card configurations.

## Temperature, fans and measurement coverage

The continuous 1 Hz observer spans idle periods, loading, hardware probes and
inference. Its recorded peaks are distinct from the helper's per-case phase
readings, which can catch shorter events.

| Measurement boundary | PNY 5070 Ti | ASUS Prime 5070 Ti |
|---|---:|---:|
| Continuous observer: peak GPU-core temperature | 77°C | 63°C |
| Continuous observer: peak intended fan duty | 65% | 42% |
| Continuous observer: peak reported board power | 300.87 W | 287.48 W |
| Recorded case/phase GPU-core maximum | 77°C | 64°C |
| Observed hardware/software thermal-throttle samples | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

The observer used 78°C warning and 83°C pause thresholds. No sampled warning or
thermal-throttle event occurred in the normal-run capture segments. Power-limit
activity is reported separately and is not thermal throttling. Driver fan duty
does not verify physical fan RPM. GPU memory and hotspot temperatures are
unavailable.

Sampling gaps and the reboot interval remain explicit; no temperatures are
interpolated across them. Monitoring interruptions are separate from
overtemperature events. One-Hz samples can miss shorter peaks, and this workload
does not establish cooling capability at uninterrupted maximum board power.
Different card positions and uncontrolled ambient conditions prevent treating
the temperature difference as an isolated board-design comparison.

The single-PNY baseline lacks the newer structured per-GPU breakdown, but its
legacy one-board fields retain 76 single-client case readings with a 65°C
maximum and 78 whole-case readings with a 68°C maximum. These historical
boundaries remain separate from the dual-card channels.

## Standalone communication and placement study

The [two-card communication and placement study](docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md)
records 153 unprofiled inference conditions, three separate traces, transfer
samples and workload-specific recommendations. Those diagnostic observations
remain separate from this normal benchmark cohort. Conditions overlapping
background activity retain an explicit confound flag.

## Limits and related reports

These are one-pass engineering observations. Automatic clocks, ambient
conditions, filesystem caches, natural stopping lengths, endpoint transport and
runtime allocation policies limit causal and statistical conclusions. A shared
model ID or public configuration fingerprint does not authenticate identical
weight bytes or effective server behavior. Failures remain part of the dataset;
unavailable readings are not zeros. No intelligence or model-quality benchmark
was performed as part of this hardware comparison.

See [measurements and sessions](docs/measurements.md), the
[mixed-card comparison](docs/5070-plus-5060-comparison.md), and
[sharing results](docs/sharing-results.md) for metric boundaries, recorded-condition
selection and public exports. The
[multi-GPU communication study](docs/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement.md)
describes the separate diagnostic methodology and its measured coverage.

## Complete campaign thermal boundary

A separate frozen capture through 2026-11-04 00:24 UTC includes the normal
cohort, standalone diagnostics, loading and idle periods. Adjacent valid samples
cover approximately 7.077 hours per card across four segments; the reboot and
sensor gaps are excluded. Later GLM work is outside this boundary.

| Observation | PNY 5070 Ti | ASUS Prime 5070 Ti |
|---|---:|---:|
| Valid temperature samples | 25,196 | 25,195 |
| Sampled GPU-core maximum | 77°C | 67°C |
| Maximum intended fan duty | 65% | 42% |
| Peak reported board power | 302.04 W | 287.48 W |
| Samples at or above 78°C / 83°C | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Hardware / software thermal-active samples | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Software power-cap-active samples | 1,667 | 133 |

Power-cap activity is distinct from thermal throttling. These sampled maxima do
not bound unsampled peaks, memory or hotspot temperature. No heat value is
interpolated across gaps, and case energy is not recalculated from these samples.
The 83°C interlock also limits what this experiment can establish about
unrestricted continuous operation.

![Complete campaign GPU-core temperatures](results/aggregates/two-5070-ti-campaign-temperature.png)

![Complete campaign intended fan duty](results/aggregates/two-5070-ti-campaign-fan.png)

and [coverage summary](results/aggregates/two-5070-ti-campaign-thermal-summary.json)
retain the recorded segment boundary.

## docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md

Canonical source: [docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md](docs/two-5070-ti-placement.md)

# Two RTX 5070 Ti cards: communication and execution strategies

Two equal-capacity GPUs benefit different workloads differently. On this
i7-5960X / 64 GiB Windows machine, balanced layer placement substantially
improves long-context LFM and Qwen inference. Gemma E2B's equal split instead
causes a severe decode regression. Independent instances improve concurrent
job throughput when each instance fits comfortably on one card.

These standalone llama.cpp diagnostics are separate from the
[180-case LM Studio/native Strata comparison](docs/two-5070-ti-comparison.md).
They do not replace historical measurements or enter normal Wattever aggregates.

## Protocol and coverage

The hardware is a PNY RTX 5070 Ti and ASUS Prime RTX 5070 Ti, both 16 GB,
with NVIDIA driver 617.42. The standalone build is llama.cpp b12058,
commit `3f8af15a7`, executable SHA256
`ff552b19fe6038bd45a00ead5e4a8d49422e3d6735cfc9672acc34b0c9767115`.
Nsight Systems is 2026.3.2.476.

| Measurement family | Recorded coverage |
|---|---|
| Transfer microbenchmarks | 280 conditions: 14 routes, 10 sizes from 4 B to 256 MiB, two timing modes |
| Inference screening | 153 unprofiled conditions |
| Instrumented inference | Three separate Gemma traces |
| Inference outcomes, including profiles | 146 successful, six unsupported, three failed, one allocation failure |
| Background-activity overlap | 19 conditions retained with an explicit confound flag |
| Measured inference repeats | One per measured condition; unsupported/failed attempts remain separate |

The main inference matrix uses the same existing GGUF files, F16 K/V,
Flash Attention, reasoning off, MTP off, temperature 0, top-p 1 and seed 73129.
Prompt targets are 512, 20k and 80k, with one or two clients and a 256-token
maximum output budget. Actual counts and natural EOS remain recorded.
Per-slot context is target plus 5%, 512 headroom and the output budget, rounded
up to a multiple of 256. Batch/ubatch sizes are 2048/512, with eight CPU and
batch threads. Each fresh engine has an excluded short warmup.

All requests use explicit IPv4 with prompt caching, idle-slot caching and
context shifting disabled. Historical localhost timings are unchanged.
Backend prompt-evaluation timings remain separate from client prompt tokens
divided by TTFT. Filesystem-cache equality and complete mapped-weight residency
are unverified. Q8 K/V and fixed-output closeouts are separate treatments.

Socket/inactivity timeout is 900 seconds per request, with a 920-second wait
per awaited concurrent future, then cancellation and worker cleanup. This is
not a hard 900-second whole-condition deadline. Unsupported or failed attempts
remain in the evidence; their token rates are not treated as successful runs.

Two-card power is integrated once over the shared client-group interval.
Single-card execution includes the installed idle second board. Whole-case
GPU joules per output token include prompt processing; decode-phase joules
per token have a different boundary. Neither measures wall-socket system power.

## PCIe paths and transfer measurements

Both GPUs negotiate **PCIe Gen 3 x16 under load**. The 256 GB NVMe remains
installed. OS device/parent relationships are recorded, but physical motherboard
slot labels and undocumented NVMe lane sharing are unverified. An idle lower
generation is not reported as the loaded link.

CUDA peer access is **false in both directions**. The cross-card probe below
explicitly stages through portable-pinned host RAM. A CUDA peer-copy API name
does not establish direct physical P2P transport.

Rates are median validated joint payload GB/s at 256 MiB per route. Simultaneous
rates use an actual shared barrier-to-completion interval; independent rates
are never added and presented as simultaneous throughput.

| Route | Mixed 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti | Two 5070 Ti |
|---|---:|---:|
| Pinned RAM to GPU0 | 13.57 | 13.58 |
| Pinned RAM to GPU1 | 6.88 | 13.56 |
| GPU0 to pinned RAM | 10.42 | 10.39 |
| GPU1 to pinned RAM | 7.08 | 10.42 |
| Explicit staged GPU0 to GPU1 | 2.37 | 1.77 |
| Explicit staged GPU1 to GPU0 | 4.66 | 2.37 |
| Simultaneous equal RAM-to-GPU routes | 13.77 | 13.96 |
| Simultaneous 2:1 RAM-to-GPU routes | 19.69 | 19.47 |
| Simultaneous GPU-to-RAM routes | 14.12 | 20.42 |
| Bidirectional staged cross-card routes | 7.68 | 11.31 |

The second card's host link improves, while these particular one-way staged
microcopies do not. This is evidence against treating link width alone as a
complete predictor of cross-card performance. Dispatch, context handling,
synchronization and the unpipelined DtoH-then-HtoD route are included.
Small-transfer host latency likewise is not intrinsic PCIe hardware latency.
The raw samples retain sizes, copy counts, direction, validation and timing mode.

Sustained sequential local-VRAM controls measured **375.66 / 384.24 GB/s** of
copied payload by CUDA events on PNY/ASUS, with approximately 80 ms batches.
Short host-timed microcopies measured 162.03 / 17.15 GB/s under a different
protocol. Those short figures do not establish degraded ASUS memory bandwidth.
Payload bytes are counted once; a separate read-plus-write traffic convention
would double the accounting, not the measured payload rate.

Monolithic host-pinning and concurrently held pooled allocations are separate
controls. The pooled 8 + 8 + 2.75 GiB sequence succeeded and was released.
This does not prove identical behavior for a production Runtime API allocation
inside an already loaded model process.

## Single-request prefill and decode

Values below are observed **prefill / decode tok/s**, using client timing.
All rows use one client and F16 K/V. Balanced means a 1:1 layer split.
The output-count column makes stopping differences explicit.

| Model / quant | Prompt target | PNY only | Balanced two-card | Actual output tokens, PNY / balanced |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LFM2.5-24B, QAD-Q4_0 | 20k | 6,934 / 183.39 | 8,965 / 173.72 | 256 / 256 |
| LFM2.5-24B, QAD-Q4_0 | 80k | 1,792 / 83.69 | 7,405 / 129.38 | 256 / 256 |
| Qwen3.8-27B, UD-Q3_K_XL | 20k | 1,853 / 45.54 | 2,853 / 45.31 | 250 / 250 |
| Qwen3.8-27B, UD-Q3_K_XL | 80k | 449 / 1.41 | 2,010 / 36.42 | 221 / 221 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Q4_K_M | 20k | 456 / 59.45 | 5,697 / 138.59 | 244 / 215 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Q4_K_M | 80k | 386 / 50.20 | 4,882 / 113.22 | 234 / 233 |
| Gemma 4 E2B, Q4_K_M | 20k | 11,049 / 190.66 | 9,703 / 31.93 | 256 / 256 |
| Gemma 4 E2B, Q4_K_M | 80k | 7,304 / 152.66 | 5,645 / 10.60 | 246 / 246 |

LFM's 80k case improves prefill 4.13 times and decode 1.55 times, with equal
actual output counts. Qwen27 improves prefill 4.47 times and decode 25.82 times,
also with equal counts. Qwen35's differing EOS lengths require descriptive
interpretation: its table is not an exact-output paired latency or energy claim.
The CSVs retain strict comparisons separately from common-budget observations.

The final allocation logs also change materially at 80k/one client:

| Model | PNY-only CPU_Mapped weights, GiB | Balanced CPU_Mapped weights, GiB | Additional evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| LFM | 1.571 | 0.200 | Logged host-expert policy in the single-card condition, absent in balanced |
| Qwen27 | 3.283 | 0.509 | Single-card CPU KV buffer 1.297 GiB; balanced KV 2.594 GiB on each GPU |
| Qwen35 | 8.509 | 0.266 | Logged host-expert policy in the single-card condition, absent in balanced |

These observed allocations support a capacity/placement explanation for the
long-context gains. They do not isolate a doubling of GPU compute. CPU_Mapped
bytes alone do not establish which pages were physically resident, how much
CPU work occurred, or whether the pagefile was accessed.

## Gemma placement and communication

Gemma's equal split is slow despite ample combined VRAM. A reverse 1:2 split
with physical device order ASUS then PNY places more of the shared-tail weights
on PNY. It changes several placement variables, so this is an intervention on
the whole layout, not an isolated KV-cache experiment.

| Gemma condition | 20k prefill / decode | 80k prefill / decode |
|---|---:|---:|
| PNY only | 11,049 / 190.66 | 7,304 / 152.66 |
| Equal layer split | 9,703 / 31.93 | 5,645 / 10.60 |
| Reverse ASUS:PNY 1:2 | 11,989 / 141.27 | 9,507 / 111.66 |

At 80k, the reverse layout's whole-request wall time is 10.68 seconds for 246
output tokens. It improves total latency despite slower decoding than PNY
alone. For sustained generation, the single-card decode rate remains higher.
Its GPU energy is a separate objective: ASUS alone records 11.15 J/output token
including prefill, versus 13.06 for the reverse layout at that workload.

The three whole-workload traces record approximately 1.86 GB, 102.80 GB and
3.53 GB of logical/requested CUDA copy bytes for single, equal and reverse
placement. These are **not measured physical PCIe bytes**. Profiles overlap
background download activity, have unquantified instrumentation overhead and
are excluded from ordinary rankings. Summed API wait durations are not wall
idle percentages; client/trace phase clock alignment is unverified.

Final positive allocations, rather than dry-fit logs, govern placement claims.
The recovered profiled console records have the same observed final allocation
shapes as their corresponding plain runs. Equal aggregate buffers do not prove
identical placement for every individual tensor.
A CPU_Mapped buffer does not prove CPU computation, pagefile traffic or physical
residency. Shared weight placement alone does not verify every KV tensor's
locality. The trace and layout evidence support a communication/waiting
explanation, but do not isolate a single causal mechanism or quantify phase
idle time. Gemma's six tensor-mode cases failed an actual split-axis assertion;
the classic-row closeout reported unsupported split buffers.

## Concurrent throughput and energy

Aggregate output is total actual output tokens divided by one shared group
interval, including prefill. Independent instances run one request on each GPU.
They are not a sum of standalone token rates.

| Model / prompt | PNY with two clients | Shared balanced model | Independent instances | Output-count qualification |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| LFM, 20k | 45.99 | 69.79 | 117.77 | 256 + 256 for all three |
| LFM, 80k | 2.43 | 13.65 | 9.84 | 256 + 256 for all three |
| Qwen27, 20k | 4.26 | 20.83 | 30.21 | Different EOS lengths; descriptive |
| Qwen27, 80k | Timed out | 3.23 | 1.03 | Different EOS lengths; descriptive |
| Gemma E2B, 20k | 67.96 | 23.95 | 143.03 | Different EOS lengths; descriptive |
| Gemma E2B, 80k | 11.47 | 4.62 | 34.85 | Different EOS lengths; descriptive |

LFM at 20k illustrates independent-instance throughput: 2.56 times the PNY
two-client rate with equal output counts. At 80k, sharing one model across both
GPUs is faster than duplicating it. Capacity and context change the best choice.

| Objective | Supported setting / limit |
|---|---|
| Lowest total request latency | Balanced LFM/Qwen at long context; Gemma reverse layout at 80k. Consult exact-output buckets. |
| Highest concurrent job throughput | Independent instances for LFM at 20k; balanced LFM at 80k. Gemma favors independent instances under the common-budget observations. |
| Largest tested model/context | Successful 80k screens are recorded, not true maxima. Qwen27 single-card two-client 80k timed out; balanced two-card execution succeeded. |
| Lowest measured GPU energy | Workload-specific: LFM80k balanced 17.63 versus PNY 26.82 J/output; Qwen27 80k balanced 93.42 versus 165.79, both including prefill and with matched output counts. |

Equal, unequal and experimental tensor execution were tested on the Qwen/LFM
models. Architecture, recurrent state, KV layout and backend restrictions mean
support is not interchangeable across models. A clean, successful case is
required before recommending a mode. The background-confounded Qwen35 tensor
and independent conditions remain observable but have no clean recommendation.

## Counters, limits and reproduction

Per-card power, energy, VRAM, utilization, clocks and core temperature were
captured. Sampled driver PCIe RX/TX and WDDM dedicated/shared allocations are
available. The Nsight collection did not request CPU stack/context-switch
sampling, PCIe hardware-byte counters or WDDM residency/page-fault traces.
Memory/hotspot temperature is unavailable. Driver rate samples and global
paging counters cannot establish per-model spill or physical PCIe bytes.

No usable Linux CUDA/vLLM environment was established, and no OS or driver
change was made. The named GGUF files were reused; bounded header/directory
hashes and sizes are recorded, while full-file byte identity is unknown for
some historical files. One-pass results, cache state, natural stopping and
clock variation limit causal and statistical interpretation.

For a new standalone balanced one-client 80k condition, a representative
PowerShell recipe is below. Choose a free port and your own model path; stop
other model engines through their owning applications first. The command is a
standalone llama.cpp recipe, not a Strata lifecycle command.

```powershell
$env:CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER = 'PCI_BUS_ID'
$env:CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES = '0,1'
& .\llama-server.exe --model $model --host 127.0.0.1 --port $freePort `
  --ctx-size 84992 --parallel 1 --kv-unified-per-slot 84992 --kv-unified `
  --cache-ram 0 --no-cache-idle-slots --device CUDA0,CUDA1 --main-gpu 0 `
  --split-mode layer --tensor-split 1,1 --gpu-layers auto --fit on `
  --fit-target 1500 --flash-attn on --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 `
  --spec-type none --reasoning off --no-cache-prompt --no-context-shift `
  --slots --offline --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 512 --threads 8 `
  --threads-batch 8 --log-colors off --log-timestamps --verbose --perf
```

The JSON/CSV artifacts linked below preserve actual arguments, counts, samples,
validation, timing methods and comparison exclusions. Private paths and
persistent device identifiers are omitted in public derivatives.
